product.plus: The headline love: an interface where starting, stopping and resuming a task takes seconds. You can start the timer before even naming the entry, and a home-screen widget begins counting in one tap without opening the app.

product.title: Mandatory sign-up: you can't even peek inside without an account
product.minus: People are put off that you can't see the app without handing over your data — no local storage, no demo. For a time tracker, a forced login plus a marketing opt-in reads as data harvesting and instantly kills trust.

product.title: "Free" with a catch: a month of premium, then a paywall
product.minus: A frequent grievance: the app presents itself as free, silently enables a premium trial, then after a month hides basic things (report export, viewing old data, others' hours) behind a ~€10/mo subscription. People feel baited.

product.title: Cluttered, unintuitive UI for simple needs
product.minus: For people who just want to "start a timer and see hours", the mobile UI feels like a chaotic pile of text and buttons. Many admit the web version is excellent — it's the app, trying to do too much at once, that frustrates them.

product.title: Login buttons dead, constant logouts
product.minus: A painful class of bugs: the Sign in / Sign up, SSO and Apple buttons simply don't respond (only Google works), and after an update the app keeps kicking users out. Logging back in mid-workday is agony.

product.title: Sync breaks: "you're offline" and lost hours
product.minus: Trust in a tracker is undermined when it loses sync with the web and stubbornly shows "offline" with a live connection, or even drops already-recorded hours. For a tool where the data is a client's money, that's critical.

product.title: "You were removed from a workspace" bug locks out new users
product.minus: A brutal first-run bug: a brand-new user gets stuck on a message that someone removed them from a workspace that doesn't exist. "Try again" and "create workspace" buttons do nothing — there's no way in at all.

product.title: Pomodoro with no end-of-session sound — a years-old bug
product.minus: Many love the built-in Pomodoro, but it has an annoying hole: the sound plays only at the start of a session and break, not at the timer's end, so you can't tell when it's done. Users note the bug has lingered for three years.

product.title: Cross-platform: phone and desktop, seamless
product.plus: What keeps people for years: the same tracking lives seamlessly across phone, PC and browser, with effortless switching between devices. For people who work wherever they are, that's the decisive advantage.

product.title: Generous free tier covers real needs
product.plus: Despite the paywall gripes, many are won over by how much the free plan gives: reports, weekly goals, no ads. For personal tracking by students and freelancers, the free tier is enough without any subscription.

product.title: Projects, tags and reports reveal where time goes
product.plus: A strength for those who stay: flexible categorization by project, client and tag, plus clear reports and weekly goals. People say they finally saw their patterns for real and became more productive.

product.title: Bank sync is the headline paid feature, and it keeps breaking
product.minus: People buy premium specifically for automatic bank sync, and it dies after a couple of days, throws credential errors, or simply stops refreshing records — for months on end with no fix.

product.title: Support ghosts you, and bugs sit unresolved for years
product.minus: Even premium users have no working support channel: the BudgetBakers team acknowledges a bug but leaves it broken for 3, 6, 11 months, replies with canned messages, or vanishes after the first email.

product.title: You can't make a top-level category — only a sub-sub-category
product.minus: The app forces its own bloated category list: you can only add a new one nested under a sub-category, and you can't delete or rename the existing ones — everyone's spending is structured differently, and it frustrates even fans.

product.title: A clean, simple, visual interface — the main reason people love it
product.plus: The app's core strength: a screen that's clear at a glance, intuitive charts and pie diagrams of spending by category; people keep it as a daily tool for years and recommend it freely.

product.title: Manual entry works great — the app is useful even without a bank
product.plus: Many users deliberately enter expenses by hand and are happy: it's easy to categorise spending, spot overspending per category, and keep a budget overview, and the free version covers all the basics.

product.title: Bank coverage is thin: outside the US/EU your bank often just isn't listed
product.minus: Users from India, Mexico, Indonesia, Kazakhstan, Vietnam, Qatar and elsewhere buy premium for sync — then find their bank or country isn't supported, with no warning before they paid.

product.title: Data vanishes: sudden logouts, disappearing records, sync duplicates
product.minus: The scariest class of complaint: the app logs you out on its own and your data won't reappear on re-login; records come and go, and sync either spawns duplicates or stalls with a 'Cloud Sync Deadlock'.

product.title: The lifetime license is a beloved alternative to endless subscriptions
product.plus: For those whose sync works, the option to pay once for lifetime access instead of a perpetual subscription is a real draw — cited directly as the reason to switch from competitors like YNAB.

product.title: Premium banners and upsell notifications clutter the home screen
product.minus: Constant premium banners on the home screen and intrusive pop-ups spoil the experience; it gets absurd — notifications arrive offering to 'upgrade my lifetime license to a lifetime license'.

product.title: Exchange rates are fixed and don't update, multi-currency is half-baked
product.minus: Exchange rates are hard-coded and won't pull live values, and changing a rate retroactively rewrites the whole history; separate two-currency accounting and the rates tab have stayed unfinished for years.

product.title: Forced login and online-banking access — with no offline mode
product.minus: Some people just want a private offline tracker, but the app forces an email login (wiping old records) and asks for online-banking username/password/OTP to import — a dealbreaker at onboarding.

product.title: Lag, freezes, and regressions after every update
product.minus: Complaints about sluggishness, freezing report tabs and blank screens, plus the sense that every update breaks something: search stops finding anything, or a breaking login regression lands on Android.

product.title: Years-long loyalty: "the only one I always come back to"
product.plus: The core of the 5-star reviews are people who've used it for 2-10 years: the first thing they install on a new phone, an indispensable daily tool for lists, tasks and notes.

product.title: Ads pop up instantly and get in the way while you're typing
product.minus: Ads greet you right at launch, flood the screen and intrude while typing and reading; for a note app that feels absurd.

product.title: Pricey subscription instead of a one-off purchase puts people off
product.minus: The price to remove ads and unlock basic features is a monthly or yearly subscription ($40/yr, £6, Rs 2600), not a one-off; many would pay once but won't subscribe.

product.title: Notes vanish on sync and when switching phones
product.minus: After a sync or a move to a new phone, people lose years of accumulated notes — they end up in the trash, in an empty app, or gone entirely.

product.title: Cursor jumps to the end of the document after every keystroke
product.minus: When editing a long note the app keeps snapping the position to the end or top of the document, forcing you to scroll back — a real obstacle for heavy writers.

product.title: Rating prompt pops up before you've even used it
product.minus: The app asks for a rating right after install, before you've tried anything; some users read this as a red flag and a trick to farm stars.

product.title: Consent screen hands your data to hundreds of ad vendors
product.minus: A pop-up offers to share your data with hundreds of third-party vendors, with toggles on by default — this drives privacy-conscious users away and gets the app uninstalled.

product.title: Calendar and widgets keep your whole life in one place
product.plus: The combo of calendar, notes and home-screen mini-widgets is a top loved feature: appointments, medications, shopping lists and tasks all at hand — something even Google Calendar doesn't give.

product.title: Color-coding and category tabs make notes easy to find
product.plus: Splitting notes into category tabs, colors and emoji on the nav bar is exactly what people praise: everything stays neat, organized and quick to find.

product.title: Free version is generous, yet locks basics behind the paywall
product.minus: Premium hides things that feel basic: undo, changing background color, auto-sync, saving images, bold text — and that frustrates even users who are otherwise happy.

product.title: Missing formatting: bold, fonts, size, text color
product.minus: Even happy users ask for basic formatting — bold, underline, font and text-color choice, highlighting; its absence especially hurts writers and long-note keepers.

product.title: Simplicity and speed are the main reason people don't leave
product.plus: The app is praised for being simple, fast, lag-free and unbloated: opens instantly, buttons in the right spots, search with highlighting — exactly what's needed for quick notes.

product.title: Shifts vanish on their own
product.minus: The most common pain: logged shifts disappear — after a reboot, after a new entry, sometimes just overnight. For an app people use to track money owed for hours worked, this strikes right at trust.

product.title: An update wipes out years of history
product.minus: An update promises to transfer the data but instead erases everything or breaks the migration. People lose months and years of records — for long-time users this is the most painful scenario of all.

product.title: Disarming simplicity is the main love
product.plus: Most happy reviews praise the same thing: the app does exactly one job — count hours — and does it simply, quickly and clearly. No bloat, a true 'less is more'.

product.title: It works out your pay from the rate
product.plus: The key value beyond a plain timer: enter your hourly rate and the app works out earnings per day, week and pay period. People use it to check their employer's math and avoid being short-changed.

product.title: Export and printing locked behind paywall
product.minus: Without the paid version you can't export a report or PDF — yet sending the log to an employer is the whole point for many users. The free version without export feels like 'just a note on my phone'.

product.title: Too few rates for multiple jobs and holidays
product.minus: The app caps out at one or two rates, but people's reality is messier: evening, night, weekend and holiday rates, a second job, a day rate. The single most common feature request is more slots for different rates.

product.title: Editable shifts save the forgetful
product.plus: A strength for people on manual time-keeping: even if you forget to clock in, you can go back and set the real time after the fact and add a note to the shift. That's what makes it a reliable replacement for paper timesheets.

product.title: The UI redesign made it worse
product.minus: A recent redesign broke familiar habits: checkboxes on the left gone, notes collapsed into tiny cells, shift view showing every other day. Some long-time users are asking for a 'classic mode' back.

product.title: Suspicious pop-up sites and 'virus' scares
product.minus: An alarming signal: pressing 'new shift' or 'punch in' sometimes opens random sites screaming 'your phone is infected'. For a tracker entrusted with work data, this badly undermines its reputation.

product.title: Paid 'Pro' gets lost when you switch devices
product.minus: The purchased premium is hard to restore: after a new phone, a reinstall or a fresh Android, Pro won't install and people don't know how to get back what they paid for. The lack of cloud bites here too.

product.title: No ads and no cloud clutter
product.plus: People specifically value that the free version doesn't bury them in ads and demands no accounts or logins: install and go. For many that's the direct reason they pick it over dozens of other trackers.

product.title: Accidental shift reset with no undo
product.minus: Fragile UX: one wrong tap zeroes out a day's work, with no undo button. Sometimes a manual-entry window pops up by itself, and leaving it erases the punch-in time.

product.title: An ad after every entry turns a 10-second log into minutes
product.minus: To add a single dish, a free user sits through one or two full-screen video ads (often with no close button — you have to open the advertised app's Play Store page to skip), then several more screens pushing premium. This happens after every meal.

product.title: Duolingo-style gamification enrages people who just want to count calories
product.minus: The yeti mascot, streaks, chests, diamonds and a daily "I'm committed" tap feel like kindergarten, not an adult tracker. There's no way to turn it off, even with premium, and many leave for competitors because of it.

product.title: An endless onboarding quiz — dozens of questions before you see the app
product.minus: Before you can use it you must answer 50+ questions (down to how many kids you have and what clothes you'll wear after losing weight), with no skip option. Many delete the app before ever reaching the tracker. Worse, the survey repeats if you skip a few days.

product.title: Aggressive subscription pushing and a "free" trial that isn't
product.minus: After onboarding you hit a paywall and can't test the key features. The rigged "discount" spin wheel, fake free-trial advertising and full charges instead of the promised price all read as dark patterns.

product.title: AI photo recognition systematically undercounts calories
product.minus: The headline feature works poorly: the AI confuses ingredients, can't judge portion size, and consistently undercounts calories by 30-40% versus manual entry. For a calorie tracker that's not just inaccurate, it's potentially dangerous.

product.title: You can't turn off tips and animations even on the paid plan
product.minus: After every logged meal come "meal tips" and unskippable animations that slow you down. Users have begged for a settings toggle for years, and the devs answer "by design". Some note that the "swap this for something healthier" advice triggers eating disorders.

product.title: Recent updates broke the app: black screens, freezes, "no connection"
product.minus: In spring 2026 paying users report en masse that the app won't load, hangs on "Get Started", or shows "no internet connection" all day on a working Wi-Fi. There's no offline logging — a server outage locks you out of even your already-entered data.

product.title: Basic features locked behind the paywall — free users can't even see the day's log
product.minus: Many find it absurd that the free version hides the day's details, weight trend, or fiber. Returning users discover that features that used to be free — and even their own contributed food data — are now paywalled.

product.title: A huge food database and a clean, pretty interface — what users genuinely love
product.plus: The standout strength is the broad database (you can find almost any product), a working barcode scanner, and a pleasant, intuitive design. Even the angriest reviews admit it's functionally the best calorie tracker out there.

product.title: It genuinely works for weight loss — those who stay drop the kilos
product.plus: For users who survive the onboarding and ads, the app delivers: staying in a deficit gets easier, and people report losing 9-21 pounds in a couple of months. For some, the streaks actually do help with motivation.

product.title: Support replies fast, and disliked features do sometimes get fixed
product.plus: Despite the overall anger, a notable share of reviews are edits up: the team issues refunds, replies quickly in chat, and added an option to snooze meal tips for two weeks — which people reward with a higher rating.

product.title: No proper reports or data export — a dead end for serious trackers
product.minus: Paying users complain about the lack of weekly/monthly summaries, file or API export, and history beyond a couple of years. You can't hand your food diary to a doctor or dietitian — for an 84€ app that becomes a deal-breaker.

product.title: Notes vanish, with no way to get them back
product.minus: The most painful and frequent complaint: notes disappear, end up in trash, duplicate, or get irreversibly deleted — sometimes including protected, important records people relied on.

product.title: Once-free features moved behind a subscription
product.minus: Long-time users are furious: custom notebook covers, colour coding, fonts, reminders — the very things they chose the app for years ago — suddenly became premium-only.

product.title: Cross-device sync is unreliable
product.minus: Notes don't reach other devices, sync duplicates or overwrites entries, shows a false last-sync time — for people working across phone and PC it kills the app's whole point.

product.title: Laggy and crash-prone even on simple notes
product.minus: Each update makes the app heavier: it's slow to load even one-line notes, freezes and crashes — galling for something meant to be a quick notepad.

product.title: Forced sign-up and phone-number demand scare users off
product.minus: You can't even try the app without an account, and sign-up demands a phone number — for a notes app that feels suspicious, and people uninstall on the spot.

product.title: Pushed AI annoys and raises privacy fears
product.minus: AI-feature ads creep into the notes themselves, and many don't want AI accessing their private thoughts; for a grocery list it's simply unwanted.

product.title: Paid version underdelivers, with no real support
product.minus: Subscribers complain the promised features don't work, refunds aren't given, and 'priority support' replies with templates or is unreachable — some call it a scam.

product.title: Logging in often fails — access to notes is lost
product.minus: A stuck login buffer, an expired SSL certificate, a code window that loops on reload — users get locked out and cut off from their own notes, especially on a new phone.

product.title: Beautiful design and pleasant note organisation
product.plus: What users love most: an elegant, tidy interface, colourful notes and cover-bearing notebook folders that make organising your thoughts a pleasure.

product.title: The best free Evernote alternative, with migration
product.plus: Many arrived fed up with paid Evernote and are delighted: built-in migration pulls over thousands of notes, and the ad-free 5 GB free tier does what rivals charge for.

product.title: Rich content types: text, photos, audio, handwriting
product.plus: Users value that a single note holds images, voice recordings, checklists, handwriting and formatting — combining the strengths of several apps in one.

product.title: A proud Indian 'swadeshi' app users rally behind
product.plus: A notable share of Indian users pick the app precisely because it's homegrown and back Zoho on principle, calling out the lack of ads and a sense of data safety.

product.title: Ads injected over the podcast — even for paying users
product.minus: The app started injecting its own dynamic ads right into the middle of the track, and they remain even for people who bought the app long ago or pay a subscription. Longtime users see it as a betrayal.

product.title: Downloads break: vanish, re-download, refuse to play
product.minus: Downloaded episodes delete themselves, need several re-downloads, or throw a "file cannot be played" error even though streaming the same episodes works fine. For offline listeners this kills the core use case.

product.title: Playback jumps: rewinds, repeats, cuts out chunks
product.minus: Episodes randomly rewind a couple of minutes, repeat what you just heard, or skip large chunks — and the skipped parts can't be replayed, as if cut from the file.

product.title: Downloads gigabytes on cellular, ignoring "Wi-Fi only"
product.minus: Despite the "Wi-Fi only" setting (or auto-download turned off entirely), the app downloads gigabytes over cellular, in one case burning through 152 GB in two days.

product.title: New "playlist" replacing the familiar Up Next queue annoys
product.minus: An update removed the one-tap way to add multiple episodes to Up Next, hiding familiar buttons behind extra menus and forcing a new "playlist" concept users didn't want.

product.title: Queue and order won't stick: episodes snap back into place
product.minus: Drag an episode in the queue and it snaps back; the queue randomly empties or reorders itself, and there's no built-in way to play oldest-to-newest.

product.title: Android Auto stripped down: episode date and time-left gone
product.minus: An update removed the episode release date and time-remaining from the Android Auto version, so while driving you can't tell if an episode is new; for some, steering-wheel skip controls stopped working too.

product.title: Gone unstable: crashes, freezes, lags on launch
product.minus: After recent updates the app crashes on open or when checking for new episodes, freezes on long episodes, and now has a several-second lag between pressing play and audio even on downloaded files.

product.title: Paywall on basic features and questionable pricing
product.minus: Basic things like folders, shuffle and Wear OS support are locked behind a subscription, and people who once bought the app or were lifetime "champions" get nothing — while ~£34 a year feels steep.

product.title: Best-in-class cross-device sync: resume on any screen
product.plus: When it works, sync seamlessly carries progress across phone, tablet, web and work computer — it's exactly why longtime users stay loyal.

product.title: Clean, simple interface without visual clutter
product.plus: Fans praise the intuitive, lightweight interface with no on-screen banners, easy drag-and-drop subscription sorting, and one-thumb operation.

product.title: Huge catalog: almost any podcast is findable
product.plus: Users repeatedly note they can find nearly any podcast for any interest, and many came here as a replacement for the shuttered Google Podcasts and Stitcher.

product.title: Rich playback controls: speed, silence trimming, sleep timer
product.plus: Power listeners value per-podcast speed control, silence trimming, skip intro/outro, and the sleep timer for drifting off to a podcast.

product.title: Full-screen ad on every tap
product.minus: Ads appear when you open the app, switch to any screen, even when picking an episode — 2-3 at a time that you can't close right away.

product.title: Ads you can't close
product.minus: Often there's no close button or it doesn't work, the ad gets stuck in an endless loop — the only escape is to force-close the app or restart the phone.

product.title: Fake close buttons open the ad
product.minus: The 'X' opens the advertised site or Google Play instead of closing — users call it deliberate trickery to pad click counts.

product.title: Ads silence and stop the podcast
product.minus: Audio ads play over the podcast or pause it, and after closing playback often won't resume — self-defeating for a podcast player.

product.title: Long unskippable video ads
product.minus: Video ads of 1-5 minutes with no skip force you to wait out a timer just to pause or open your own library.

product.title: Auto-subscribing to podcasts you never chose
product.minus: The app adds and downloads episodes of podcasts the user never picked, filling up phone storage.

product.title: Skips and cut-offs inside episodes
product.minus: The player rewinds 20-40 seconds, repeats chunks and cuts off episode endings — the same episodes play fine in other apps.

product.title: Auto-launches on Bluetooth connect
product.minus: The app turns itself on and starts playing when the car connects to Bluetooth or after pausing another app, even with autoplay disabled.

product.title: Ads are a hazard while driving
product.minus: Most listen while driving, and ads now require tapping the screen to continue — users explicitly call it a safety hazard.

product.title: Paid premium still shows ads
product.minus: Users who paid for ad-free premium still get ads in podcasts, and the app keeps demanding they subscribe.

product.title: Huge catalog of podcasts and audiobooks
product.plus: The biggest library: rare and small podcasts that aren't on Spotify, plus audiobooks — the main reason people put up with everything else.

product.title: Handy playlists and offline downloads
product.plus: Building playlists, downloading episodes for offline listening, speed control and a sleep timer — praised as the best podcast player before the ads.

product.title: Responsive developers
product.plus: The team replies to messages and sometimes solves problems personally — a rarity users will add a star for.

product.title: Ads became unbearable after recent updates
product.minus: After updates the ad load exploded: spots interrupt speech every 30–60 seconds, four-minute breaks at the start, middle and end kill any immersion, and the ad volume is noticeably louder than the podcast.

product.title: Rude, blame-shifting developer replies to reviews
product.minus: Many drop their rating specifically over the tone of replies: the developer blames the users themselves, argues, responds aggressively to anything below five stars, and asks "why didn't you contact me before rating it badly".

product.title: Randomly skips and cuts off the end of episodes
product.minus: The player jumps back several minutes on its own, repeats chunks, and sometimes drops the last 10 minutes while marking the episode finished — the same files play fine in other apps.

product.title: Decade-long loyalty and an unmatched feature set
product.plus: Users keep it for 7–10 years and across six phones, calling it the best Android podcast player: huge catalog, deep customization, per-podcast playback speed and episode ordering.

product.title: Confusing, unintuitive interface
product.minus: Basic actions take trial, error and extra steps: subscribing is hard, the right buttons are hidden, and features are buried in menus — you can learn it, but not quickly.

product.title: Updates wipe subscriptions, playlists and downloads
product.minus: After updates whole playlists, hundreds of downloaded episodes and the entire subscription list vanished, leaving a "clean slate" — and downloads also disappear for no reason at all.

product.title: Pushy ad consent: hundreds of vendors to toggle by hand
product.minus: On setup there's no "Reject all" button: to opt out of targeted ads you must manually disable hundreds of "legitimate interests" and up to 305 partners — it takes up to 15 minutes.

product.title: Playback stops on its own when the screen turns off
product.minus: During chores or sleep the sound cuts off mid-sentence and won't resume: you have to grab the phone and hit play again — since a recent update it just stops playing when the screen is off.

product.title: Paid subscription doesn't remove the ads
product.minus: Premium and lifetime ad-free buyers still see ads: after the June update they returned despite a 2020 package, the premium account periodically "logs out", and audio ads remain even for paying users.

product.title: Constantly nags for ratings and battery warnings
product.minus: The app asks for a rating over and over, even after you've rated and turned off notifications, and pops up a battery-restrictions warning on every new screen you load.

product.title: Drains battery and phone storage in the background
product.minus: The app launches itself in the background whenever any media device connects, bogs down the phone, can eat over half the battery in an hour, and fills up to 90% of storage without cleaning downloads.

product.title: Responsive developer who fixes and helps fast
product.plus: Some users praise that same support: the developer replies fast, solves problems personally within a couple of emails, and keeps updating the app and adding features without breaking the core.

product.title: A free Spotify alternative with no algorithms
product.plus: Many left Spotify for it: free, huge selection, easy offline downloading, no algorithmic recommendations — just what you subscribed to, plus a buy-once-forever model.

product.title: Subscription pop-up on every open
product.minus: A full-screen "buy premium" prompt fires on every launch and even when switching back to the already-open app, with no way to dismiss it for good.

product.title: Ads remain after paying for premium
product.minus: "Ad-free" subscribers still get sponsored-podcast pop-ups and audio spots, and support replies that it is "intended behavior."

product.title: Loses your place in an episode
product.minus: After a pause, a call, or switching apps the podcast restarts from the very beginning, forcing people to note the timestamp by hand.

product.title: Garbled high-speed ad keeps interrupting audio
product.minus: Every few seconds playback cuts out for an unintelligible sped-up disclaimer, after which you must manually hit play again.

product.title: Auto-opens ad sites in the browser
product.minus: Without any tap the app launches Chrome and dumps you on sketchy "you have a virus" or gaming pages, even with the screen off.

product.title: Subscribes you to podcasts you never chose
product.minus: Unknown shows nobody subscribed to appear in the feed and have to be unsubscribed one by one.

product.title: Burns mobile data despite Wi-Fi-only settings
product.minus: Despite "Wi-Fi only" and background data off, the app spends hundreds of megabytes and even gigabytes, pushing people into their data caps.

product.title: Drains the battery in the background
product.minus: The app keeps running in the background after being closed and rapidly eats the charge, while disabling background permissions makes it unusable.

product.title: Region blocks and lost accounts
product.minus: People are suddenly cut off by country or locked out of their account, needing a VPN to sign in, while support goes silent and you cannot even export your OPML.

product.title: Deep control over downloads and playlists
product.plus: Granular auto-download, episode-order and playlist controls with offline listening — things Spotify and many rivals lack.

product.title: Huge catalog and finding any show
product.plus: Almost any podcast can be found, including niche RSS feeds missing from other platforms.

product.title: Cross-device sync and a web player
product.plus: The Play Later list and progress sync between phone and website, letting you keep listening on a PC.

product.title: Simple, intuitive interface
product.plus: The single most-praised trait: a no-nonsense, easy player that even non-techy users find intuitive and that 'just does its job'.

product.title: Huge selection of podcasts
product.plus: A vast catalogue: people find their favourite shows, niche genres and titles unavailable in other players.

product.title: Playback resets and skips on its own
product.minus: A frequent pain: episodes stop after a random time, jump back 30 seconds, or reset to the start, losing your place.

product.title: Updates break the app
product.minus: Long-time users complain that recent updates make the app worse: it hangs, won't load, crashes, and familiar features vanish.

product.title: Downloads don't work offline
product.minus: Downloads often fail to finish, hang in the queue, or a downloaded episode refuses to play without a connection — the core offline feature lets users down.

product.title: Reworked downloads list is unusable
product.minus: Downloads used to be grouped by podcast AND sorted by date; the new screen forces constant toggling and breaks 'play next'.

product.title: Played episodes don't leave the feed
product.minus: Marking 'played' doesn't hide the episode, and played/unplayed statuses periodically reset — easy to get lost and re-scroll on long-running shows.

product.title: Minimal, unobtrusive ads — for some
product.plus: Many praise that the free version's ads are rare, silent and non-interrupting, unlike Spotify and YouTube.

product.title: Ads turned loud and aggressive — for others
product.minus: The opposing camp: ads have multiplied, grown loud and aggressive, sometimes with disturbing or near-pornographic imagery that ruins the experience.

product.title: Podcasts vanish and stop syncing
product.minus: Favourite podcasts randomly disappear, new episodes don't show for weeks, and the feed stops syncing — even though other apps show them fine.

product.title: Crashes and dropouts during background play
product.minus: The app crashes or cuts audio when minimised, when switching apps, or when the screen dims — background playback is unstable.

product.title: Forced AI features drive users off
product.minus: Emails about adopting AI and updated terms trigger churn among loyal users — many see it as 'AI slop' and targeted ads rather than value.

product.title: Support and billing go unanswered
product.minus: Support requests get no human reply (only automated AI emails), and cancelling a subscription sometimes doesn't stop charges — users feel ripped off.

product.title: An ethical, money-free escape from Spotify
product.plus: Many arrive as refugees from Spotify and YouTube: free, no corporate strings, no paying 'the other guys'.

product.title: Beloved sleep timer
product.plus: The sleep timer earns its own affection: it helps people fall asleep to podcasts, especially noted by insomniacs and parents.

product.title: Recording and publishing misbehaves
product.minus: Creators are let down by the studio side: guests' voices break up while recording, drafts can't be found or published, edits don't save, and livestreaming was removed.

product.title: Episodes skip, repeat, and cut off the ending
product.minus: The single most common complaint: playback randomly jumps back, replays what you already heard, and ends episodes early. Manually scrubbing doesn't fix it, and it has been broken for a long time.

product.title: Completely free, no ads, no subscriptions
product.plus: The top reason people love it: entirely free, no banner ads, no paywalls, no nagging subscription popups. Users flock here from Spotify, Apple Podcasts and YouTube purely for clean listening.

product.title: Simple, clean interface with no clutter
product.plus: The design wins praise for being minimal and clear: no clutter, no forced content feed, everything where you expect it. Many love it precisely for the lack of distracting recommendations.

product.title: Deeply customizable and feature-rich
product.plus: Under the hood there's a wealth of options: playback speed, silence trimming, download filters, customizable swipes, search by country and by guest name. People keep discovering new features for years.

product.title: Open source and volunteer-run inspires trust
product.plus: The FOSS nature is a value in itself: no trackers, no data harvesting, users donate and praise the community. For many it's a deliberate escape from "billionaire apps".

product.title: The beloved replacement for the shuttered Google Podcasts
product.plus: After Google Podcasts and other players shut down, AntennaPod became the go-to rescue: recommended, migrated to, and kept — especially for offline listening.

product.title: Download management is confusing, auto-deleting old episodes fails
product.minus: The Inbox / Downloads / Queue system confuses people, and the expected "keep N newest, delete older" option is either missing or doesn't work, so storage fills up — some uninstall over it.

product.title: Weak Android Auto integration
product.minus: In Android Auto the player won't auto-advance to the next track, won't release audio when you switch sources, and keeps playing past the episode's end — switching manually while driving is dangerous.

product.title: Notification and watch play button sometimes won't respond
product.minus: Out-of-app controls are flaky: the play button in the notification shade or on a smartwatch won't fire, forcing you to open the app itself to start the episode.

product.title: Playback spontaneously stops every few minutes
product.minus: For some users the podcast pauses on its own every 5–10 minutes and they have to restart it manually — annoying, though it doesn't happen every time.

product.title: Learning curve: not obvious at first
product.plus: The Inbox/Queue concepts and overall logic confuse people at first — several rated it low until they got the hang of it, then bumped it up to 5 stars.
product.minus: Newcomers struggle: the interface and organization take time to learn, and some users had previously deleted the app out of frustration.

product.title: Heavy battery drain in the background
product.minus: A few users report abnormal background battery use — one saw 50 minutes of background playback eat three times the battery of 40 minutes of screen-on time in another app.

product.title: Audio jumps back and cuts off the ending
product.minus: Episodes randomly jump back 30 seconds to several minutes and replay what you just heard, and that same time is then cut off the end — it happens on almost every podcast.

product.title: Playback stops on its own mid-episode
product.minus: The podcast goes silent after a few minutes and won't resume until you open the app and hit play; tweaking background and battery settings doesn't help.

product.title: Deep customization and playlists
product.plus: The most flexible app in the category: manual playlists, auto-adding new episodes, trim beginning and end, playback speed, tags — power users keep coming back precisely for this.

product.title: Ad banner shifts the buttons and causes mistaps
product.minus: The bottom banner loads with a delay and pushes the timeline and play/pause buttons up — as you reach to pause you hit a random spot on the scrubber or the ad itself.

product.title: Paid ad-free version still plays ads
product.minus: People bought ad removal, yet podcasts still get inserts every 10 minutes that aren't in the same episodes in other apps — meaning the app itself injects them.

product.title: Downloads fail and restart from zero
product.minus: The download manager keeps failing, won't resume from where it stopped and re-downloads the episode from 0% — wasting double or triple the data and forcing manual restarts.

product.title: All-in-one: radio, RSS and YouTube
product.plus: Beyond podcasts it pulls in internet radio, news RSS feeds, YouTube channels and local audio files in one place — for many it's a single replacement for several apps at once.

product.title: Artwork and player stuck on the previous episode
product.minus: In the notification shade and on the lock screen the title and artwork stay from an earlier episode — only the time and progress bar update, so you can't tell what's actually playing.

product.title: Casting to Chromecast barely works
product.minus: The Cast icon comes and goes, the connection drops mid-episode and desyncs — you often have to force-restart the app just to connect at all.

product.title: Slow, freezing and crashing after updates
product.minus: Launch takes several seconds, lists take forever to load, the app freezes while navigating and crashes — users agree it gets worse with every update.

product.title: Locked out: sign-in keeps failing
product.minus: Google sign-in doesn't work, password reset won't accept the new password, and after reinstalling subscriptions and history are gone even when you appear to be logged in.

product.title: Search can't find even the exact title
product.minus: You type the exact podcast title and it's not in the results, even though Google shows it's on Podcast Republic; you end up scrolling a hundred results or searching in another app.

product.title: Playlist jumps around and won't auto-play the next episode
product.minus: In playlist mode the app, after an episode, jumps not to the next one but to an old unfinished episode or a random spot in the list, or won't start the next at all — continuous listening breaks down.

product.title: Downloaded episodes vanish on their own
product.minus: Downloads disappear after a day or two even with auto-delete off — people end up with an empty list on a plane or offline.

product.title: Playlist is broken: can't remove items or play through
product.minus: Removed episodes come back, added ones don't appear, and you can't play the whole list through — only one episode plays, then it stops.

product.title: Jumps back to the start of an episode
product.minus: Minimize the app or let the screen go dark and the episode restarts from the beginning; progress is lost mid-listen.

product.title: Crashes and won't open after updates
product.minus: After a recent update the app crashes on launch or won't open for days; reinstalling sometimes wipes all saved podcasts.

product.title: Downloads never finish
product.minus: An episode is marked downloaded but stops midway and won't play offline; even auto-download over Wi-Fi silently fetches nothing.

product.title: Auto-plays the next episode against settings
product.minus: Even with autoplay off the app starts the next episode — a real problem for people who listen to sleep podcasts.

product.title: Broken on Android Auto
product.plus: For some, Android Auto still serves them well and runs smoothly in the car.
product.minus: In the car you can't fast-forward or pick an episode from the screen, new podcasts don't sync, and only a full restart from the phone fixes it.

product.title: Ads everywhere, and paid removal doesn't stick
product.plus: Many praise how minimal the ads are in the free version — far fewer than rivals.
product.minus: Some users are buried in ads on open, and paying to remove them often changes nothing or resets after a phone wipe.

product.title: OPML import/export doesn't work
product.minus: Importing subscriptions via OPML hits a "permission required to get the file list" error that doesn't exist in phone settings — migrating from another app is impossible.

product.title: Best Google Podcasts replacement
product.plus: After Google Podcasts shut down, people tried many apps and settled here — they even find obscure subscriptions their old players lacked.

product.title: Rich catalog finds even obscure shows
product.plus: The catalog is huge and free: people find nearly all their niche and obscure shows, which was a pleasant surprise.
product.minus: Occasionally a show you want loses its episodes and the page comes up blank.

product.title: Simple interface, loved by learners
product.plus: The clean, easy interface is praised as one of the best among podcast apps; many use it to learn English and other languages from podcasts and news.
product.minus: Some still find the interface clunky and thin on features compared with rivals.

product.title: A wall of ads — 15 in a row
product.minus: Users report 11-15 back-to-back ads between a pair of songs, sometimes '20-30 min of commercials' — more than on regular FM.

product.title: Ads cut into the middle of a song
product.minus: Ads override the live broadcast and cut songs off mid-play — pausing, switching stations, or a text notification instantly triggers a commercial.

product.title: The app launches itself
product.minus: After being closed, the app starts radio on its own — while charging, at night, mid-task; many were forced to uninstall it.

product.title: Podcasts play out of order
product.minus: After an episode autoplay jumps to an old or already-heard one instead of the new one; marking 'listened' changes nothing and you can't build a queue.

product.title: Huge station selection for free
product.plus: Loved for gathering live stations from across the country and world in one free app — you can hear your hometown radio from anywhere.

product.title: Doesn't remember your place in a podcast
product.minus: It doesn't track which episode you left off on, so every time you have to scroll to find your spot — especially painful while driving.

product.title: Drops on network switch and loses audio
product.minus: Switching from Wi-Fi to mobile doesn't just hiccup — the stream is fully lost; stations hang on loading and downloads won't play offline.

product.title: A subscription doesn't remove ads
product.minus: People pay for premium and still hear ads, while the price was bumped from $9.99 to $11.99 — and they're unsubscribing.

product.title: Pads your playlist with its own tracks
product.minus: On the free tier it injects other songs into your own playlist and replays tracks you thumbed down, ignoring your choices.

product.title: Drains battery and runs in the background
product.minus: It drains the battery hard even on a downloaded podcast and constantly lingers in the background, begging for permissions and popping back up after closing.

product.title: Geo-locked — your station isn't available
product.minus: It can't find your local station or blocks the broadcast as 'outside the approved area', serves stations from the wrong country, and breaks with a VPN.

product.title: A lifeline at work and on the road
product.plus: Valued as a simple free way to hear favorite shows and music while driving, in a work truck, or at home — especially where regular radio reception is weak.

product.title: Episode restarts from zero after a pause
product.minus: Pause it or switch to another app, and the episode jumps back to the very start with no saved position.

product.title: Too many ads inside episodes
product.minus: Ads run several times per short episode, sometimes back-to-back and unskippable — the app stacks its own on top of the show's.

product.title: Favorite podcasts vanish from the library
product.minus: After updates or with no warning, favorites, listening history, and whole shows a user followed for years simply disappear.

product.title: Downloads won't play offline
product.minus: Downloads either hang forever or refuse to play without a connection, and sometimes the app seems to lie about an episode being downloaded at all.

product.title: Playback cuts out and stalls on its own
product.minus: Episodes stop mid-listen for no reason, get stuck buffering, or crash out — especially dangerous while driving.

product.title: Queue and play order are broken
product.minus: Queued episodes don't play one after another, play only the last few seconds, or run in reverse order, and Add to Queue got buried in settings.

product.title: Search and catalog miss the podcasts you want
product.minus: Search often returns nothing, there's no smart typo correction, and half the popular shows just aren't in the catalog.

product.title: Uploading your own episodes fails
product.minus: Creators go weeks unable to publish a finished episode: the upload aborts within seconds and support stays silent.

product.title: Constant pop-ups begging for a review
product.minus: The rate-the-app window pops up many times an hour and keeps nagging even after a review has already been left.

product.title: An easy platform to create a podcast
product.plus: Creators praise the easy show setup, clear mixer, and simple upload with good stats — for many it's been their home for a decade.

product.title: Rich choice of niche content
product.plus: Listeners find rare shows here — religious lectures, true crime, local radio — that aren't on the big services.

product.title: Censorship and removed podcasts drove away part of the audience
product.minus: Users accuse the service of deleting whole shows and accounts and leave, calling it a free-speech violation.

product.title: There is effectively no free tier — only a trial
product.minus: Ads promise "free", yet on opening nearly everything is locked: people can't even try the app without subscribing or handing over card details, and they call it false advertising.

product.title: Charged during the trial, then can't cancel
product.minus: The most frequent money complaint: people cancel within the trial window but still get hit with the full annual charge, and the app "won't allow" cancellation — they read it as outright fraud.

product.title: Cancellation is buried behind dark patterns
product.minus: Unsubscribing means clicking through several "are you sure?" screens with a tiny cancel button, or hitting a "something went wrong" error — users explicitly call out dark UX from an app that's supposed to be about calm.

product.title: Support goes silent and refunds are nearly impossible
product.minus: When a disputed charge happens, people wait weeks or months for any reply: the chatbot is useless, there's no phone number, and Google and PayPal bounce them back to Calm.

product.title: Too expensive for what you can get free on YouTube
product.minus: At $70–200 a year the price feels out of proportion: for sleep sounds and white noise people find free alternatives on YouTube, Spotify or Alexa and don't see what they're paying for.

product.title: The anxiety-critical content sits behind the paywall
product.minus: What stings most is that the emergency stuff — an SOS-for-anxiety meditation or panic session — is exactly what's locked: people compare it to running an ad before a video on how to perform CPR.

product.title: Cluttered UI makes finding anything stressful
product.minus: Navigation and search are a mess: the basic breathing exercise is buried in Discover → Tools, searching "mindfulness" returns 7000 identical "daily calm" results, and in a moment of distress you simply can't find what you need.

product.title: The "Take a deep breath" splash enrages on every launch
product.minus: The unskippable "Take a deep breath" splash hangs on a blue screen and reappears every time you reopen the app — the opposite of calming, and for some it even triggers PTSD.

product.title: Constant crashes, freezes and stuttering audio
product.minus: Even paying long-time users hit the app freezing on "three dots", cutting stories off at night, stuttering audio or looping on the login screen — especially after updates and on newer devices.

product.title: The content is genuinely life-changing — the core reason to love it
product.plus: Despite everything, long-time users keep it for years and say it helped with sleep, anxiety, panic attacks and even trauma — for many it's part of their daily routine and a genuine "lifesaver".

product.title: Sleep stories and narrator voices put you out in minutes
product.plus: The standout loved feature is the sleep stories and narrator voices (Tamara, McConaughey): people fall asleep before the story ends and listen to them nightly for years.

product.title: Rich variety: meditations, soundscapes, breathing, kids section
product.plus: What wins over those who stay is the variety and quality: guided meditations, soundscapes, breathing exercises and a strong kids section — something to match whatever mood you're in.

product.title: AI content and celebrity focus disappoint
product.minus: Some long-time users feel it's degrading: "Daily Calm" is AI-generated with robotic audio, and there's a focus on big-name celebrities over actual substance; a few uninstall purely over the amount of AI content.

product.title: The custom "personalised plan" turns out to be empty
product.minus: People are drawn in by an EMDR/sleep quiz promising a personalised program, but after paying and handing over data they get the same generic recommendations — and the data they gave never carries over.

product.title: The bot check and login lock people out entirely
product.minus: Getting in requires a hold-to-verify "I'm human" check that loops on "try again", plus login bugs and Google sign-in incompatibility — some people can't even create an account and uninstall before starting.

product.title: Pushy upsells and pop-ups during the actual sessions
product.minus: Even premium subscribers get bombarded with "upgrade to Family" pop-ups, upsells and notifications mid-meditation — irritating and at odds with the whole point of calming down.

product.title: After updating, the app freezes on the orange smiley and won't open
product.minus: The single most common pain: after the May update the app gets stuck forever on the splash screen with the orange face. Reinstalling, clearing cache, rebooting the phone — nothing works. Paying subscribers are left with no access for weeks.

product.title: Forced update loops endlessly: 'update' → store → 'open' → 'update' again
product.minus: The app demands an update, sends you to the store where the latest version is already installed showing 'Open' — you open it and it demands an update again. An inescapable loop that survives cache-clearing and reinstalls.

product.title: Mid-session crashes: meditations and sleepcasts cut out exactly when you need them
product.minus: Sessions die halfway through — sometimes silent, sometimes with an error, sometimes the sleepcast cuts out overnight. For a relaxation app this is fatal: you have to open your eyes to check if it crashed, which destroys the whole point.

product.title: Everything behind the paywall: even the basic breathing exercises that used to be free
product.minus: Headspace used to offer a free intro course and breathing basics — now literally everything is locked except a one-minute intro. You can't even try a technique without starting a trial. The free tier has become a gallery of padlocks.

product.title: A 'free trial' that charges you immediately, with no refund
product.minus: Users report that signing up for a '7-day free trial' charges them right away, and cancelling doesn't stop the charge. Support refuses refunds and points fingers at Google. For people with anxiety and money worries, it stings especially hard.

product.title: A cluttered Netflix-style interface where you can't even find today's meditation
product.minus: The home screen used to show the day's meditation right away — now it's a tile-heavy feed you doomscroll like social media. Search returns junk, favorites hide in a tiny widget. The paradox: an app about mental clarity overwhelms you itself.

product.title: The app keeps logging you out, especially at the worst possible moment
product.minus: Headspace regularly logs you out and demands a password — sometimes at 3am during insomnia, sometimes throwing an error when you try to sign back in. No biometrics. A paying subscriber ends up locked out of their own app.

product.title: Downloaded content won't play offline — the point of downloading is lost
product.minus: You can download meditations, but they won't launch without internet, and updates sometimes wipe all your downloads. On a plane or off-network the app is useless — for travelers, a direct reason to leave.

product.title: Andy Puddicombe's departure and the shift to an 'American' tone feels like losing the soul
product.minus: Long-time subscribers tie the decline to Andy leaving in 2022: the new voices feel less soothing, sometimes 'shouty' and inauthentic, and some content is now voiced by lifeless AI. The app, they say, 'lost its way.'

product.title: The Ebb AI chatbot and pushy upsells where people are seeking calm
product.minus: Nobody asked for an AI therapist: Ebb asks repetitive questions, is capped at 30 minutes, and often crashes, while support has been reduced to a useless bot. On top of that, constant prompts to buy more — even for active subscribers — directly contradict the relaxation premise.

product.title: When it works, the content is genuinely life-changing and best-in-class for sleep
product.plus: Despite the bugs, people adore the core of Headspace: Andy's guides finally 'make meditation click,' sleepcasts put you under in five minutes, and years of practice genuinely lower anxiety. Many write 'changed my life' and keep the subscription for exactly this.

product.title: Sleepcasts are the main reason to pay, but they lack filters and length control
product.plus: Sleepcasts and soundscapes are the flagship — the reason many keep the subscription for years and fall asleep to them nightly. Requests for filters (rain, ocean), track queuing, and a gentle alarm are 'wishes for a favorite,' not grievances.

product.title: The content is great, but the app is slow and takes forever to load every track
product.minus: Even short of a full crash, the app is sluggish: startup takes minutes, any track loads painfully slowly, and it sometimes claims 'you're offline' on fast internet. Heavy, storage-hungry, and it takes forever to render the UI.

product.title: Support via an AI bot that loops you around and never gets you a human
product.minus: When the app breaks access or billing, help has been reduced to an AI chat that ignores pleas for a human and sends you in circles. Especially painful for those who get Headspace via an employer or insurance and pay a lot.

product.title: Data harvesting under 'wellness': dark privacy settings and selling into ML/ads
product.minus: Users are alarmed by the new privacy policy: the content of their messages is collected 'to power machine learning and personalize ads,' and the opt-out is hidden and won't stick on the first try. For a mental-health app, it reads as betrayal.

product.title: Mandatory onboarding on every open with no way to skip
product.minus: Skip the app for a couple of weeks and it force-marches you through an intake survey about goals and interests — no skip button, no working back button. Often the only way out is to fully close the app.

product.title: Forced streaks and «I'm committed» you can't turn off
product.minus: After every session you must tap «I'm committed» and pledge a daily streak — no X, no «no thanks». The Duolingo-style gamification grates on people who came for peace, not pressure.

product.title: A maze of screens before and after a session instead of «open, meditate, leave»
product.minus: It takes 5-10 screens to reach the timer and as many again to close a session: «how do you feel», «your intention», «save», «tip the teacher». Slow lotus animations make it worse — people can't fit in a quick meditation between tasks.

product.title: A huge free library for any mood and any moment
product.plus: Thousands of meditations, talks, music, breathwork and yoga from world-class teachers — much of it free. There's always something to match your mood, the time of day and the exact need.

product.title: A simple, customizable timer with gongs — the reason many stay
product.plus: Many came just for the self-guided timer: custom durations, start/end gongs, interval bells every few minutes, none of Android's irritating default drones. Perfect for yoga, stretching and silent practice.

product.title: Relentless premium upselling drowns out the point of meditating
product.minus: The moment a session ends, a pop-up pushes an upgrade; before it starts, an unasked-for free trial. The constant «buy premium» right when you've found calm reads as greed and disrespect.

product.title: Core playback features moved behind the paywall
product.minus: The free version can no longer seek, rewind, repeat a track or set intervals — all locked behind a subscription. Users see it as deliberately breaking the basics to squeeze money from the people who need it most.

product.title: Audio cuts out mid-session and mid-playlist at night
product.minus: After recent updates, sleep and meditation audio randomly stops: rain cuts out in the night, playlists freeze after two hours, sessions auto-end early. For people who listen to fall asleep, it breaks the core use case.

product.title: Bookmarks, playlists and saved items vanish after updates
product.minus: Successive updates wipe folders, bookmarks and playlists or bury them so deep they can't be found — forcing you to re-search every track. Years of curation just disappears, sometimes along with your streak after a sudden login prompt.

product.title: Constant UI reshuffling forces you to relearn it every time
product.minus: The layout and home screen get overhauled almost monthly: buttons move, sections shuffle, handy new features get added then yanked. Every update means hunting for where everything went.

product.title: Genuinely helps with sleep, anxiety and building the habit
product.plus: For many it's a daily anchor over years: it helps them fall asleep, manage anxiety and insomnia, and build a lasting practice. People recommend it to therapists, friends and patients and say it changed their lives.

product.title: Trial billing: charges with no warning and no way to cancel
product.minus: Trials silently flip to paid: the promised reminder email never arrives, an annual charge lands out of nowhere, and refunds are refused even for clearly accidental sign-ups. Some users find charges for a subscription they never agreed to.

product.title: Login and accounts break: «system error», lockouts, no sign-in
product.minus: The app keeps demanding re-login, logs people out every couple of days, or greets them with a server error. After a reinstall the opening screen often has no «sign in» option at all — just a questionnaire that spawns a fresh empty account.

product.title: Streak mechanics punish missed days and can harm wellbeing
product.minus: The streak can't be switched off, and losing it over one missed day feels like «failure» — sometimes driving people away entirely. For a meditation app, these retention-game mechanics work against the very idea of calm.

product.title: Annual auto-renewal charges a year later, after the user has long forgotten the app
product.minus: The single most common complaint: people tried the trial, dropped or deleted the app, and a full year later get hit with a $60–123 charge with no email warning. The yearly-only billing turns 'forgot to cancel' into a major surprise expense.

product.title: Playback stops mid-meditation and won't resume when you press play
product.minus: A widespread recent bug: audio freezes after 8–15 seconds or a few minutes, and the play button does nothing — you have to restart the whole session. It's worst for sleep, where the sound dies overnight. Clearing cache and reinstalling don't help, and the promised 'post-holiday' fix never lands.

product.title: Charges keep coming even after cancellation, and refunds are near-impossible
product.minus: People cancel and the card still gets charged, sometimes for years. Refund requests get ignored, met with 'we can't find your email,' or flatly refused — driving users to freeze cards, dispute with their bank, and file cybercrime complaints.

product.title: Charges for an app the person never installed or subscribed to
product.minus: A distinct cluster: users get charged $69–75 for a subscription they say they never signed up for — sometimes for an app not even on their phone. It reads as fraud and erodes trust more than any bug.

product.title: Free access used to exist — now everything is paywalled and loyal users are locked out
product.minus: A classic bait-and-switch: people who for years used a couple of free sleep sounds or shared the free-year link now hit an un-closable subscription popup. Free content is gone, and many simply can't afford the 40–85€/year price.

product.title: Ofosu's voice and the guidance are the main reason people get hooked
product.plus: The most common compliment: a calm, 'not hokey' male voice (Ofosu) people want to come back to daily. The guidance is praised as gentle, consistent, and beginner-friendly — the voice is what turns the app into a daily habit.

product.title: Teaches meditation from scratch through structured plans — not just a dump of hundreds of tracks
product.plus: Many arrived as skeptics who'd never meditated, and the step-by-step plans (Foundations, beginner courses) actually taught them the practice. The skill progression — and not repeating instructions once you've advanced — is a repeated highlight.

product.title: Personalization and a meditation for every situation feel seamless
product.plus: Users value that the app adapts to their goals and mood, asks questions at the start and mid-plan, and offers a meditation for nearly any situation — anxiety, sleep, focus, kids, walking, shower — without the overwhelm of Calm or Headspace.

product.title: Sleep sounds and soundscapes help people drift off — until a bug or crackle ruins them
product.minus: People love the sleep sounds (rain, thunderstorm, brown/white noise) and use them nightly — but these break the most: playback dies when the screen sleeps or the app is minimized, the hour timer gets stuck, and Deep Sleep and Sound Asleep develop a 'crackling' noise. For anyone who paid purely for background sound, it makes the purchase worthless.

product.title: Cancellation is buried behind a long, deceptive 10-page 'fake' flow
product.minus: Users describe a deliberately confusing cancel flow: a 10-page sequence that tricks you into thinking you've already unsubscribed, instead of a simple redirect to Google Play. There's no cancel button on the subscription page — which in several countries is outright illegal.

product.title: Too much talking in the meditations — the guide gets in the way of actually meditating
product.minus: Some experienced practitioners complain the narration is near-constant and repetitive, with no toggle to dial down how much the guide speaks. Others add that the meditations feel same-y ('visualize a beach') and amount to instructions rather than silence.

product.title: No monthly option and (now) no lifetime — yearly-only pricing prices out low-income users
product.minus: People love the content but the pricing model pushes them away: there's no monthly tier, the one-time lifetime option was removed, and the lump-sum yearly charge is out of reach for those on fixed incomes. It especially stings that the yearly price ($70) now exceeds what lifetime access used to cost ($60).

product.title: Progress, streaks, and the calendar don't log correctly, sapping motivation
product.minus: Gamification cuts both ways: a tracking bug fails to log completed sessions (especially sleep), streaks get out of sync, and there's no way to reset progress or change your goal. For some, the sparse badges (jumping from 30 days straight to 365) demotivate them enough to quit.

product.title: People love the content, but the app falls apart
product.minus: The most common refrain: the courses and teachers deserve five stars, but the app itself is awful. People drop to 1-2 stars purely for the app, while explicitly praising the content.

product.title: You can't cancel — the app crashes on "Manage Subscription"
product.minus: The loudest pain point: trying to cancel, tapping "Manage Subscription" force-closes the app. People try dozens of times, email with no reply, and end up cancelling the card through their bank.

product.title: After updates the app crashes on launch
product.minus: Every update breaks the app: it crashes on open, and the only fix is an endless uninstall-reinstall-relogin loop. Android and Samsung owners complain most.

product.title: Video and audio buffer and cut out — even on fast internet
product.minus: On 100+ Mbps connections videos buffer every few seconds and meditations randomly pause. You can't finish even a two-minute clip or get through a meditation in peace.

product.title: Paid in full — but no access, asked to subscribe again
product.minus: Money debited, annual plan paid — yet the app deems it 'cancelled' and demands a fresh trial. Courses stay locked for weeks while support stalls.

product.title: Expensive, almost all paywalled, and the 'free' ads mislead
product.minus: The $299-588/year price shocks, and you only learn it after 20 minutes of setup. Previously free sounds and meditations are now locked too, and the 'free' promised in ads turns out to be a lie.

product.title: They keep charging after you cancel and remove the card
product.minus: People disable auto-renew and delete their card details — yet still get charged, sometimes on a new card they never provided. Refunds are refused, citing just-updated policies.

product.title: Support is an AI bot — no way to reach a human
product.minus: Instead of humans, a looping virtual assistant that can't understand questions, broken WhatsApp links, and ignored emails. One non-committal reply a day at best.

product.title: Streaks reset — meditations don't get counted
product.minus: Months-long meditation streaks drop to zero after an update or crash, and minutes sometimes don't log at all. For a daily practice that stings.

product.title: No background play or audio-only mode — the screen sleeps and the lesson restarts
product.minus: Turn off the screen or switch apps and the meditation stops and starts over. For audio lessons and eyes-closed meditation that's killer — and it burns battery and data.

product.title: Downloaded lessons won't play offline
product.minus: The download feature is useless: saved videos and meditations won't play offline or crash the app. Plan to listen on a flight and you're left with nothing.

product.title: The content genuinely changes lives — star teachers across every area
product.plus: Fans call it the best investment they've ever made: courses cover every area — money, relationships, health, spirit — with world-class author-teachers. Many pay for years and see real shifts.

product.title: A huge catalog of courses, meditations and a real community
product.plus: Users love the variety and depth: there's a quest for any need, you can work on several areas at once, and there's a motivating community of like-minded people and teachers around it.

product.title: The redesign buried what people loved: everything got chaotic and hard to find
product.minus: After the update navigation fell apart: favorite meditations are buried under layers of menus and "courses", search is illogical, and the layout is cluttered. Long-time users say an app meant to calm them now causes anxiety.

product.title: Playback randomly cuts out mid-session
product.minus: Meditations stop at random mid-way, often right at the five-minute mark, and to resume you have to back out and find your spot again. It hits sleep users hardest: instead of relaxing, you get dead silence and frustration.

product.title: Can't log in or register: login bounces back with an "undefined error"
product.minus: The update logged people out and they can't get back in: login loops to the same page or throws an "undefined error", and password resets don't fire. For people who need the app right now to fall asleep, it's especially painful.

product.title: Genuinely free from a non-profit — no paywalls, no ads
product.plus: The single biggest reason people love it: all content is open with no subscription and no ads, just an occasional gentle donation prompt. Against Calm and Headspace locking everything behind a paywall, it feels like a rare honest gesture.

product.title: Quality of the guided sessions and a pleasant voice keep people loyal
product.plus: Almost no one faults the content itself: the meditations are well-planned, easy to follow, with a good talk-to-silence ratio, and the guide's voice is calm and not patronizing. Many have used it for years and rate it above paid rivals.

product.title: The update wiped progress, favorites, and beloved meditations
product.minus: The move to the new version reset years of progress and favorites lists, and some old meditations simply vanished or were renamed. It's hardest on families with neurodivergent kids whose bedtime routines depended on those sessions.

product.title: Won't load and hangs on an endless loading screen
product.minus: Since the relaunch the app often won't open at all: an infinite spinner, "an error has occurred", outright crashes. Restarting, clearing cache, and reinstalling don't help — sometimes it fails to load for weeks.

product.title: Forced sign-up and a quiz before you can even see the app
product.minus: Just to try it you now must create an account, hand over your email, and complete an unskippable smiley-face quiz. For people who opened the app while stressed, those hoops are reason enough to delete it and move to a rival that asks for none of it.

product.title: Default-on background music that drags on after the session ends
product.minus: The new default background music distracts many, and after a meditation ends it keeps playing with no closing bell — so you wait or reach for the phone, breaking the relaxed state. It's especially disruptive to sleep sessions.

product.title: Downloaded meditations disappear and offline mode is hit-or-miss
product.minus: The download button often doesn't work and no longer shows whether a file finished, and already-downloaded meditations get deleted without warning. So offline sessions break the moment Wi-Fi drops — the very thing offline mode is for.

product.title: Female-voice preference is ignored — all kids' meditations are male
product.minus: Despite setting a female-voice preference, meditations play in a male voice and the promised toggle isn't there. It especially upsets parents whose kids fell asleep to a specific female-voiced session for years and now can't get it back.

product.title: Genuinely helps with anxiety, sleep, and focus — say long-term users
product.plus: Those who stay describe concrete results: it calms the nervous system, helps them fall asleep and get back to sleep after waking, and brings focus. Many were sent by psychologists and doctors, and it becomes a daily ritual for years.

product.title: Content goes deeper than rivals: not just meditations but a theory of mind
product.plus: The core reason people love it — the app teaches the 'why' and the 'what', not just the 'how'; theory, philosophy and practice together deliver something Headspace or Calm don't.

product.title: The 28-day intro course actually teaches you to meditate from scratch
product.plus: For beginners the intro course makes meditation 'click' where years of trying other apps failed — it eases you into the practice and locks in the habit.

product.title: The price stings: $150-160 a year, double the alternatives
product.minus: A ~$150 yearly sub (some were quoted up to $300) feels like a rip-off for meditation; many walk away to cheaper apps without ever trying it.

product.title: Everything is paywalled — not a single free session to evaluate
product.minus: You're forced to create an account and commit a card before you can try anything; zero free content reads as dishonest and a waste of time.

product.title: Sam Harris the person drives people away: hard to separate his politics from the practice
product.minus: Many love the content but can't meditate to a man whose politics (Palestine, trans issues, censorship) they find appalling; there are literal pleas for a 'version without Sam'.

product.title: Buggy, freezes and crawls — especially at login and offline
product.minus: Freezes at startup/login, endless installs, crashes after sign-in and no real offline mode — technical reliability repeatedly fails.

product.title: Cancelling the subscription and deleting the account is nearly impossible
product.minus: You can't cancel in-app (laptop only), the 'delete account' button is dead, and people get charged after cancelling — it reads as a deliberately predatory trap.

product.title: Sam's voice and delivery relax some and grate on others
product.minus: A chunk of users find Harris's voice off-putting and his speech too fast, too wordy and too complex — it literally snaps them out of meditation.

product.title: After the intro course there's no clear path — beginners get lost in the library
product.minus: A huge library with no structured roadmap: once the 28-day course ends, beginners don't know what to do next and feel lost.

product.title: Genuinely life-changing and builds a daily meditation habit that sticks
product.plus: The most frequent praise — the app genuinely changed lives and let people sustain a daily practice for the first time, where other apps and attempts had failed.

product.title: Scholarships and discounts make the app accessible to the broke
product.plus: Despite the steep price, the team grants free 'scholarships' and discounts without hassle to those who can't pay — and many call it out gratefully.

product.title: Support is responsive, friendly and fast
product.plus: Customer support (Karl gets named repeatedly) replies fast, in a human way and actually solves billing and tech issues — a real bright spot amid the cancellation complaints.

product.title: Too advanced for beginners: 'meditate without a head' and 'the self is an illusion' alienate
product.minus: Billed as a starting point, the course veers into advanced non-dual techniques ('you have no head', 'the self is an illusion') mid-way, and groups of beginners quit around the same day.

product.title: No captions or text for the audio — hard to follow and absorb
product.minus: Lectures and theory are audio-only with no text or captions, so some listeners struggle to grasp the dense content — a recurring request for transcripts.

product.title: Sync and playback-progress saving keep breaking
product.minus: Listening progress doesn't save and resets to 00:00, history disappears, and desktop and mobile don't sync — small but nagging glitches even for paying fans.

product.title: The teachers are the core value: many voices, many styles
product.plus: Again and again people come back for the variety of teachers — you can pick a voice and an approach to match your mood that day. Joseph Goldstein, Sharon Salzberg, Oren and others are named by name as the reason to love the app.

product.title: Nothing new — old content gets repackaged into short clips
product.minus: The single most common pain among long-time subscribers: no fresh meditations in over a year, and «wisdom clips» are just snippets cut from old material. Once you've worked through everything, there's nowhere to grow, and many flatly say they won't renew.

product.title: The best app for a meditation beginner
product.plus: The «explanation first, then practice» format and short sessions make the entry gentle — many reviews come from total beginners who finally built a regular practice for the first time. It also suits experienced meditators who want light guidance.

product.title: Dan Harris leaving is felt as losing the app's soul
product.minus: Dan Harris — the co-founder whose book and life story the app is built on — is gone, and for many that's the turning point: his podcasts and courses disappeared, engagement dropped, and some now follow him on his personal site instead.

product.title: Removing podcasts angered the people who paid for them
product.minus: The podcasts (especially ad-free and downloadable) were the main reason some users subscribed — they got pulled, downloading broke, and refunds for the months already paid were refused.

product.title: $99 a year and almost everything behind a paywall scares people off at the start
product.minus: The $99/year price with nearly all content locked reads as a «money grab», especially for those who came via a book's promise of free access. The $14.99 monthly plan is hidden — you only get it by emailing them.

product.title: Constantly demands sign-in and forgets your account
