product.title: Broken navigation controls — Skip Intro, Next Episode, fast-forward
product.minus: Basic player controls fail: the skip-intro button doesn't respond, "next episode" crashes the app, and autoplay won't queue the next one. Skip Intro sometimes jumps to a random future episode entirely.

product.title: Rising price against falling quality and a shrinking catalog
product.minus: The subscription has been hiked up to double, and users directly compare it to Netflix while questioning what they pay for: content gets removed, new movies hit Amazon first, and the app glitches all the while.

product.title: Cancellation and billing are made deliberately murky
product.minus: Users complain that canceling is hard: the subscription doesn't show up in Google Play, the website won't let you cancel, and charges keep coming with no notice. Many read it as a deliberate trap to squeeze out maximum money.

product.title: The franchise catalog — the main reason people stay despite everything
product.plus: When the app works, the content is genuinely loved: Marvel, Pixar, Star Wars, Bluey, Gravity Falls and old Disney classics bring the whole family together. Many keep the subscription for years precisely for this library and the nostalgia of childhood cartoons.

product.title: A simple, family-friendly interface — when the bugs stay out of the way
product.plus: Those whose app is stable praise it for being easy: clear navigation, handy profiles, good picture quality and a family-friendly format. For many it's their main everyday app and a way to spend the evening with the kids.

product.title: You pay for the subscription and still drown in ads
product.minus: The number-one complaint: ads run even for paying users, often two-minute breaks every few minutes of show. People literally time it and conclude a third of their paid viewing is spent on commercials.

product.title: The "ad-free" tier still shows ads
product.minus: A distinct fury comes from people who paid extra for the ad-free version or got it via a phone plan: ads appear anyway, sometimes through ESPN. Users call it a lie and outright fraud.

product.title: The player constantly loses your place in a show
product.minus: A years-old bug: on resuming a series the app either restarts the episode, jumps to its last two minutes, or skips ahead to the next one. People restart the app just to fix playback.

product.title: Freezing, buffering and crashes instead of watching
product.minus: A very common complaint: endless buffering, freezes every few minutes and crashes across phone, Fire TV, Xbox and smart TVs. Users stress that other streamers work fine on the same connection while Hulu doesn't.

product.title: The Disney merger turned login into a nightmare
product.minus: After logins were merged with Disney, users can't sign in, get kicked mid-show and forced to re-login — sometimes several times a day and weekly. Some can't even cancel because they can't get in.

product.title: Content is locked behind endless add-ons and "upgrades"
product.minus: Users are frustrated that movies and shows once included now require separate add-ons, and live TV is gated behind a pricier ESPN plan. They feel pushed into paying twice over.

product.title: Casting, activation and multi-device setup are broken
product.minus: Bought on the phone but can't watch on TV; trying to activate a device hits endless steps; casting breaks and cross-device sync glitches. Simple actions become a quest.

product.title: Audio description turns itself on, and the sound misbehaves
product.minus: A known, unfixed bug: the monotone AI audio-description voice turns on even when the setting is off. Plus ads blast far louder than the show, the first seconds after a break are muted, and voices don't match lips.

product.title: Billing is opaque: overcharges, a hidden payment page, no way to cancel
product.minus: Complaints about inflated auto-charges, double billing and being unable to cancel. The payment page is hard to find and often throws 404s, and support is effectively unreachable.

product.title: Navigation and UI lag behind rivals
product.minus: The interface is called confusing: hard to find a specific episode, easy to accidentally exit a show, no skip-intro button, and autoplay cuts off the ending to push the next one. Often compared unfavorably to Netflix.

product.title: A huge library and next-day streaming — this is what people love
product.plus: Despite all the app gripes, fans praise the vast selection of shows, movies and series, new episodes the day after airing, and originals like The Handmaid's Tale. Many watch Hulu nearly every evening.

product.title: Strong for anime and sports — but live streams collapse mid-game
product.plus: Anime fans rate Hulu's subs and dubs above Crunchyroll, and sports viewers value the live games and playoffs. It's a genuine strength of the library.

product.title: Servers buckle on the World Cup's marquee matches
product.minus: The defining failure: on the big matches (Argentina vs Algeria, Spain) the server goes down, and paying viewers simply can't open the stream.

product.title: You paid, yet the app keeps demanding you buy the package again
product.minus: The active package isn't detected: every time they try to watch, users are sent back to buy access again, even though the money is already gone.

product.title: Login drops every session, and the OTP won't go through
product.minus: Every exit forces a fresh login with OTP, and the correct code is often rejected as wrong — you spend half the match logging in and out.

product.title: «Content unavailable» — the app simply won't open
product.minus: Often it never even reaches the video: on launch you get «content unavailable» or «something went wrong», and you can't even reach the menu.

product.title: The legal stream looks worse than a pirate feed
product.minus: Even when the stream does start, it's choppy, laggy, low-res (720p max on TV), and sometimes a black screen with audio only — all on a fast connection.

product.title: «Playback not allowed» 15-30 times per half
product.minus: A specific player error fires dozens of times in a single half of a live match, turning the watch into a constant reload loop.

product.title: Refund demands go unanswered
product.minus: After paying 85k rupiah and watching no matches, people demand a refund — but there's no refund option, and support and official accounts don't help.

product.title: One account, one device — TV and phone can't coexist
product.minus: A hard single-device limit: switching from phone to TV triggers «used by another device» and another OTP, and on Android TV the app sometimes won't install at all.

product.title: Rivals pull this off better
product.minus: Viewers compare directly: Vidio handled Euro 2024 and WC 2022 fine, and Mola and FolaPlay are steadier — the rights should have gone to them.

product.title: Highlights play fine — the live match doesn't
product.minus: The paradox: clips and highlights load fine, but the one thing the package was bought for — the live broadcast — is exactly what fails.

product.title: When it does work — it's good on both phone and TV
product.plus: The rare happy users note the picture is good on both phone and TV and the app has clearly improved over before — the potential is there.

product.title: You pay for the subscription and still get ads
product.minus: The single most common complaint: people already paid for the subscription, yet ads still play — and removing them costs even more. It reads as deception and greed.

product.title: A subscription doesn't unlock the films — they're still rentals
product.minus: Even with a paid subscription, much of the catalog — especially new releases and old films — is locked behind separate rental or purchase fees. Users feel the subscription buys them nothing.

product.title: Rewinding forces you to watch ads all over again
product.minus: The player handles ads atrociously: rewind a few seconds and the ads replay, sometimes several in a row. People get stuck in an ad loop just trying to find the spot they left off.

product.title: Black screen: the audio plays but the picture is gone
product.minus: A widespread bug: the video doesn't show, only audio plays, and the screen stays black. Often only rebooting the phone helps, which makes the app borderline unusable.

product.title: Constant lag, freezing and buffering
product.minus: The app is sluggish: endless loading, stuttering playback, freezes even on flagship phones. Users note that pirate sites run smoother than this paid service.

product.title: Full-screen mode and on-screen buttons are broken
product.minus: Core player elements fail: video won't go full-screen on the first tap, the control buttons won't disappear, X-Ray and the status bar bleed over the video. A fundamental part of the video player is broken.

product.title: Subtitles are clumsy and out of sync
product.minus: Subtitles are a pain to manage: presets were removed, you can't set size or style, the text with a black background covers a quarter of the screen, and captions go out of sync or stop working after you leave the app.

product.title: No gestures for brightness, volume or playback speed
product.minus: The player lacks things that are basic in 2026: no gesture sliders for brightness and volume, no playback-speed control, no proper next-episode autoplay. Competitors solved this long ago.

product.title: Paid — but the subscription shows as inactive
product.minus: People pay, yet the app insists there's no subscription; support promises a fix within an hour and vanishes. Money taken, no access — it's perceived as outright fraud.

product.title: Locked out over the device limit
product.minus: The service complains about too many devices even when only one is logged in, and locks you out for a month instead of a soft cap. The account suddenly drops from one device while staying on another.

product.title: A huge library in one place — what people love
product.plus: Those who like the service value the breadth of the catalog: lots of movies and shows, new releases and old favorites, everything gathered in one place, including kids' content.

product.title: Dated interface and broken search
product.minus: Navigation is clumsy: search returns the wrong films, sub-genre filters are gone, and reaching the right season takes a dozen clicks. The interface feels like 2003 next to Netflix.

product.title: Doesn't remember where you stopped
product.minus: The «Continue watching» section works poorly: favorite shows vanish from it, episodes restart from the beginning, and Alexa forgets your progress. Every time you have to hunt for your spot again.

product.title: Bad sound mix and out-of-sync dubbing
product.minus: The audio is unbalanced: gunshots are deafening while dialogue is a whisper at the same volume. Lips don't match the dub, and dubbing tracks from neighboring episodes get mixed up.

product.title: Downloaded videos won't play offline
product.minus: Downloads break: background downloading doesn't stop when paused and re-downloads what you already have, a download_persistence error appears, and offline clips demand internet or simply won't open.

product.title: Ads keep playing even on the premium plan you paid extra for
product.minus: People buy the top tier specifically to kill ads — yet the ads keep coming: several per episode, 45 to 190 seconds long, sometimes right before the final scene. It feels like being charged for nothing.

product.title: You pay, then it instantly demands an upgrade before you can watch anything
product.minus: The classic trap: you buy a plan for a specific match or show, open it, and the app demands an upgrade to a pricier tier. It hits World Cup subscribers especially hard.

product.title: You paid, but the app doesn't recognize the subscription and locks you out
product.minus: Money is charged (often twice), Google shows the payment, the TV works — but the phone app insists there's no subscription and pushes you to pick a plan again. Money gone, no access.

product.title: The app lags, buffers, and crashes — especially on TV
product.minus: Endless spinning circle, freezes, black screens, random crashes. Users with fast internet say Peacock is the only app that behaves this way.

product.title: It can't remember which episode or spot you stopped at
product.minus: "Continue watching" throws you back to episodes you've finished or to the start, and fixing it means scrubbing forward through even more ads. A double punishment for the player's bug.

product.title: World Cup and matches stream in Spanish only, with no English audio
product.minus: US viewers pay for the broadcasts, yet matches (especially the 2026 World Cup) are Spanish-only with no way to switch language. For many it's the deciding reason to cancel.

product.title: There's effectively no support — just AI bots and refusals to refund
product.minus: When you're charged with no access, there's nowhere to turn: live chat is broken, social channels go silent, only AI "agents" reply. Google cites a no-refund policy. The customer is left out of pocket and unhelped.

product.title: Disturbing, aggressive ads during kids' and sports content
product.minus: Horror trailers, aggressive and pharma ads pop up during soccer or kids' shows, and the ad volume is jarringly loud. Children get scared, parents are furious.

product.title: Charges after cancellation and for subscriptions never signed up for
product.minus: Double charges, billing for an already-cancelled plan, mystery installs by the provider. It reads as hidden fees and fraud.

product.title: Huge catalog: Bravo, WWE, Telemundo, sports and favorite shows in one place
product.plus: The main reason people stay: a rich mix of classics and new releases, Bravo reality, sports (motocross, baseball, the Olympics), Telemundo. Many call it their favorite streaming service.

product.title: Free or cheap when bundled with Xfinity, Walmart+ and Instacart
product.plus: For many it comes bundled with their ISP or a Walmart+/Instacart membership, and the ~19.99 annual price is praised as excellent value. Free or cheap access is a genuine plus.

product.title: Too many ads for a paid service — ad breaks eat half the episode
product.minus: Even on ad-supported tiers the load is extreme: 5 to 6 minutes of ads per 22–30 minute episode, and pausing now gets covered by an ad. People compare it to regular TV and leave for free Tubi/Pluto.

product.title: Black screen on Play — the app opens but playback dies
product.minus: The single most common pain: the user signs in, sees the whole catalog, hits play — and gets a black screen and a crash. Clearing cache, reinstalling and rebooting don't help; support blames a "known issue with Android."

product.title: The app crashes the moment you launch it or pick a show
product.minus: For a chunk of users the app doesn't even survive to the menu: it crashes on open or right after you tap a title, over and over, across multiple devices. Reinstalling changes nothing.

product.title: Constant buffering and error codes (6004, 3004, 3005) break playback
product.minus: Even when video starts, it buffers endlessly, freezes and spits out error codes — while other streaming apps on the same device and connection run flawlessly. Users explicitly pin it on Paramount's infrastructure, not their own hardware.

product.title: Lag and freezing especially hammer smart TVs (LG, Samsung, Firestick)
product.minus: On TVs the app is the slowest, glitchiest of the bunch: laggy startup, a play button stuck in the middle of the screen, frozen picture. Other services run fine on the same TV, and sometimes the app even reboots the TV itself.

product.title: Downloaded videos won't play offline — downloads require internet
product.minus: The whole point of downloading — watching on a plane or off-grid — is broken: offline, the app won't open your downloaded videos and demands a connection. It comes up repeatedly and strikes users as absurd.

product.title: Too many ads — and they run even on the ad-free / premium tier
product.minus: More ads than regular TV: several spots every five minutes, the same ones on repeat. Worse — users who paid for the ad-free tier still get ads, including during the UFC corner talk.

product.title: Impossible to cancel the subscription — endless loops and dead links
product.minus: Cancelling becomes a quest: links go nowhere, the chatbot loops you around, you're bounced between Google and the website. People report trying to cancel for months; one says it sent them to urgent care.

product.title: Forgets your place and episode — drops you on the wrong one
product.minus: The app loses where you stopped and serves up a week-old episode — or a different show entirely — as your "next." Every time you have to manually hunt down the right season and episode.

product.title: Can't sign in, and password reset on mobile simply doesn't work
product.minus: Login breaks across devices: paid on a laptop, can't sign in on the TV; "technical difficulties" for weeks. And the in-app password reset just dumps you back on the sign-up screen — you have to uninstall the app to change your password.

product.title: UFC replays are chopped up: no walkouts, no full event end-to-end
product.minus: Users who subscribed for UFC are furious that you can't watch a full event replay end-to-end: instead of one broadcast you get individual fight clips, no walkouts, no commentary, no corner segments. To get the full experience people go to YouTube.

product.title: The catalog is the main (often the only) reason people stay: Star Trek, Sheridan shows, UFC
product.plus: Users genuinely love the content: Star Trek, the Dutton Ranch / Tulsa King universe, Nickelodeon classics — and many keep the sub purely for one or two exclusives. UFC landing on the service is met with delight as a huge saving versus PPV.

product.title: When it works, users praise the price, convenience and "watch anywhere"
product.plus: For a slice of users it just works: they praise the affordable price, smooth streaming, simple interface and the ability to watch anywhere — phone, on the go, at home. To them Paramount+ is a reliable daily service they recommend.

product.title: Hard paywall: almost nothing is watchable for free
product.minus: Users sign up expecting "free anime" only to find every episode crowned and locked behind premium. That bait-and-switch feeling is the single biggest driver of the angry 1-star reviews.

product.title: Billing that steals: charges after cancelling and double payments
product.minus: People keep getting charged after cancelling, get billed twice for one subscription, and can't unlink payment. This isn't "too expensive" — it reads as outright theft from the card.

product.title: Paid — but premium never activated
product.minus: Money is taken, the confirmation arrives, yet the app still demands a subscription. Support says "wait 24 hours" then drags it out for days, with no refund.

product.title: Cancelling is impossible — the flow is broken and buried
product.minus: The cancel button bounces between the app and Google Play and never works, and you can't delete the account without cancelling first. It escalates to threats of lawsuits.

product.title: Library gaps: marquee titles simply missing
product.minus: You pay for a subscription and the iconic shows — Attack on Titan, One Piece, Tokyo Ghoul — are absent or only partly there. It hits hardest for people who came for one specific title.

product.title: Patchy dubs: series left half-voiced
product.minus: A title is tagged as dubbed, but half of it has no voiceover in your language and you can't finish the series. It stings most for the Hindi audience, where rivals do have the dub.

product.title: Region locks and VPN just for the full library
product.minus: In India, Indonesia and elsewhere only a slice of the catalog is available, forcing users onto a VPN to watch. In its country of origin the service is banned outright.

product.title: Won't load or play: endless loading and API errors
product.minus: On a solid connection it loads forever, claims "no internet", throws API 429/403 errors and green screens. You hit play and it just spins or kicks you back to the list.

product.title: Downloads break — offline viewing fails
product.minus: A queue of 8-10 episodes comes back empty, downloads only start with the app open, and files expire or buffer. The whole point of offline viewing collapses.

product.title: Player is bare-bones: no speed, gestures, or screen lock
product.minus: No 1.5x/2x (and where it exists, only up to 1x), no double-tap-to-pause, no screen lock, no picture-in-picture. Basic conveniences users expect even after paying.

product.title: Subtitles and AI translation fail; audio out of sync
product.minus: Subs vanish, drift off timing, collapse to Arabic-only, and the AI translation is woefully wrong. On top of that, chronic audio-video desync across every device.

product.title: Price goes up, quality drops — and there are still ads
product.minus: Price jumped from 7.99 to 9.99, quality suddenly drops, and even on the paid tier you still get promo trailers and popup ads. "Ad-free" effectively doesn't exist.

product.title: Huge library and near-simulcast — the real draw
product.plus: When it works, it's the best home for an anime fan: a massive catalog old and new, near-simulcast releases, plus manga. Many have stuck with it for years.

product.title: Cheap subscription and good streaming quality
product.plus: For the satisfied crowd, the subscription feels very affordable and the video quality and load speeds are excellent. That often outweighs the bugs in their rating.

product.title: Emotional attachment: a "second home" for fans
product.plus: For part of the audience the relationship is almost personal — a place of peace at the end of the day, shared family viewing across generations. That's loyalty money can't buy.

product.title: "Free" is the whole product people forgive everything for
product.plus: The core reason people love Tubi is genuinely free access to a big library with no subscription and nothing to pay. Reviewers explicitly contrast it with paid services and say they'll tolerate ads at that price.

product.title: Ads wreck the pacing: 3 minutes of film, then a block of 5-7 spots
product.minus: The single most common pain is ad frequency and length. People describe breaks every few minutes lasting 2-4 minutes, up to 6-7 spots in a row; a 90-minute film stretches to 3 hours, and some uninstall before finishing even one movie.

product.title: A huge, eclectic library — from classics to niche oddities
product.plus: The breadth and variety of the catalog wins people over: thousands of movies and shows, nostalgic cartoons, documentaries, true crime, old and new films. They often find titles missing from paid services.

product.title: Loses your progress: "continue watching" vanishes or rewinds to the start
product.minus: A painful regression: after an update the app rewinds episodes to the start after ads, drops the "continue watching" list, or demands a sign-in to keep your place. People have to hunt for where they left off every time.

product.title: Won't load, crashes, green/purple screen after updates
product.minus: Technical failures are a recurring complaint: crashes on launch, endless 15-30 minute loading, a green screen mid-movie, a blank purple screen. Clearing cache and reinstalling often don't help, and people tie the problems to recent updates.

product.title: The World Cup hook drew people in, but "free" turned out misleading
product.minus: The free World Cup 2026 promo triggered a wave of letdown: matches won't play, the feed shows stands and buses instead of the game, you can't watch on a TV, and some feel tricked into creating an account.

product.title: The ads aren't just frequent — they're harmful: gambling and adult content
product.minus: A separate, sharp grievance is what the ads contain: gambling and betting blocks (especially in Australia), sexual content, and Spanish-language spots on the English app. People call it harmful and a reason to uninstall.

product.title: No account, no hassle — a simple way into watching
product.plus: Many value that Tubi needs no account or email: open it and watch. People call the interface clear and easy to use, with simple navigation on both phone and PC.

product.title: Comfort and company: watched on the road to unwind and escape
product.plus: For some, Tubi is an emotional refuge: it helps them unwind after a long day, pass time while traveling, and for truckers eases anxiety and loneliness, while nostalgic shows bring back childhood.

product.title: The algorithm forces choices: no search, repeats, and the removed thumbs-down
product.minus: People resent the system deciding for them: search disappears and results feel random, the home page is clogged with auto-playing previews, the same show loops endlessly, and the removed thumbs-down strips their ability to filter out unwanted picks.

product.title: Quality suffers: audio desync, truncated descriptions, missing captions
product.minus: Small but persistent playback flaws grate: audio drifts out of sync and only a restart fixes it, movie descriptions are truncated with no way to expand them, captions aren't everywhere, and picture quality drops while ads run in high resolution.

product.title: Content rotates and ages: favorites vanish, people crave fresh titles
product.minus: Some are frustrated that movies and shows get pulled from the catalog, and that it skews toward old "already on TV" titles. Yet improvements are noticed too — newer releases like Godzilla x Kong are flagged as a step forward.

product.title: More ads than actual content
product.minus: Viewers repeatedly count it out: a 20-minute show stretches to nearly an hour because of ad blocks stacked several spots deep, turning watching into a test of patience.

product.title: Freezes, stalls and loses audio
product.minus: The picture locks up every few minutes, audio drifts out of sync with the lips, and a frozen ad won't even let you change the channel — all of it reportedly worse after updates.

product.title: Live TV autoplay you can't turn off
product.minus: The app opens straight into loud live TV and keeps playing while you merely browse — with no pause and no setting to stop it, which is especially maddening with kids around.

product.title: Doesn't remember where you stopped
product.minus: It loses your place in a movie or show, then forces ads on you when you try to scrub back to it; next episodes start not at the beginning but around 12 minutes in — right before the first ad break.

product.title: Won't open or connect
product.minus: For a chunk of users the app simply stopped launching or keeps insisting "check your internet connection" while every other service works fine; reinstalling doesn't help, and it reads like a mass outage on Pluto's end.

product.title: Forced sign-in for a "free" app
product.minus: People resent that a free service demands an account, a password and even age verification; sign-in confuses login with sign-up, locks you out for too many attempts, and gates content behind registration.

product.title: Ads that are mistimed and inappropriate
product.minus: Spots cut in seconds before a scene ends, repeat endlessly, blare louder than the film itself, and drop medication, horror and adult-themed ads into kids' and classic programming.

product.title: Channels and favorites keep disappearing
product.minus: Pluto pulls channels and favorite shows, resets your chosen favorites every time you switch, hides the search function after an update, and recycles the same content for weeks without refreshing.

product.title: Casting and device compatibility break down
product.minus: It runs on the phone, but casting to a TV or Chromecast brings audio desync, a black screen or crashes; on some Android devices and boxes Pluto just refuses to launch at all.

product.title: A huge free catalog of classics and live channels
product.plus: The core reason people forgive everything else: a free library of old movies, series and themed live channels so deep that many call the selection better than paid subscriptions and a full cable replacement.

product.title: The channel-surfing feel with no click barrier
product.plus: What many love is the linear format itself: channels that just keep playing recreate the classic TV experience, remove the agony of picking something, and let you channel-surf the way cable once did.

product.title: Free and reachable for those on a tight budget
product.plus: For viewers on a tight budget the free price is the whole point: Pluto stands in for pricey subscriptions and cable, gets recommended for when "money is tight," and is praised as a way to watch favorites at no cost.

product.title: Bans and «account under review» with no wrongdoing
product.minus: People get banned and stuck «under review» for days, convinced they broke no rules — and for many it means being cut off from loved ones, not a minor annoyance.

product.title: «Download official WhatsApp» — while already on the official app
product.minus: Logging in on a new phone, the app keeps demanding the «official WhatsApp» and won't verify the number even though the official version is already installed — and the user simply can't get in.

product.title: The new «WhatsApp: name» notification format irritates and hides the sender
product.minus: After the update, notifications now read «WhatsApp: sender name» — the extra logo and word push out what matters, and it's harder to see at a glance who messaged.

product.title: Crashes, black screen and overheating after recent updates
product.minus: The app crashes, sometimes hangs on a black screen after unlock, and the phone itself overheats and lags from WhatsApp — complaints spike especially after the last two updates.

product.title: Video quality in Status and on sending is auto-degraded
product.minus: Even sending in HD, users end up with blur and stutter: resolution drops on its own and Status video comes out choppy — and people ask to fix this rather than add features.

product.title: Voice-message compression ruins audio — users ask for an HD voice mode
product.minus: Aggressive voice-message compression strips out audio detail, and users explicitly ask for the same «HD» toggle already given to photos and videos.

product.title: After updates the connection drops: no calls, no «last seen»
product.minus: After an update the connection keeps dropping — no calls and no «last seen»; toggling Wi-Fi no longer helps and only a phone reboot does.

product.title: Getting logged out on its own and losing access to files
product.minus: Users get suddenly logged out without doing anything, and after logging back in files won't download or the backup only restores to an old date — losing important photos.

product.title: Watches and wearables won't sync, with no update «available»
product.minus: On smartwatches the sync fails with «something went wrong» and a prompt to update, yet no update exists in the store — leaving a freshly bought watch useless.

product.title: The chats, channels and Status UI is long overdue for cleanup
product.minus: Archived chats stay pinned on top, channels have no tab of their own, groups aren't separated from normal chats, and Status has emojis you tap by accident — small things that pile into frustration.

product.title: Built-in UPI/payments exist but are raw and nearly useless
product.minus: The payments module basically only does mobile recharge: no paying by UPI ID, no balance check, no utility bills — users feel Meta failed to build even a simple payment app.

product.title: Indispensable, simple and fast contact with loved ones worldwide
product.plus: Despite the gripes, for most it's the primary, irreplaceable way to stay in touch with family and friends: simple, fast, encrypted, with calls, voice notes and groups — without it the phone feels empty.

product.title: User idea: voice-note transcripts/translation, like Instagram has
product.plus: Users themselves suggest a valuable feature — transcribing voice notes to text (like Instagram) so you can read them afterward, plus more transcript languages such as Arabic.

product.title: Login is now paywalled: the SMS code is hidden behind a Premium subscription
product.minus: The single biggest complaint: just to log in or sign up, people are forced into a paid subscription or an "SMS fee". It used to be free, and users read it as extortion and a cynical bait-and-switch.

product.title: The verification code never arrives — and the user is locked out of their account
product.minus: Even without paying, login often breaks: the SMS or email code simply never arrives, or it's sent to an old, already-dead device. People type in their number for hours and still can't get into their own account.

product.title: Lightning speed and unlimited cloud storage — what users love most
product.plus: What earns the love: instant messaging, cross-device chat sync, and unlimited cloud where nothing is lost. Huge files send without compression, and 200k-member groups still run smoothly.

product.title: The new design with its transparent "glass" header — even fans recoil
product.minus: After the update many find the interface physically unpleasant: a distracting transparent top bar, an iPhone-like look, and no way to revert. People literally say it's become hard to use and makes them want to cry.

product.title: Support goes silent when your account is hacked or frozen
product.minus: When disaster strikes — a hack, a hijack, a freeze — support is effectively absent: days of silence, zero reaction to reports. People lose accounts, money and private data with no one to turn to.

product.title: Downloaded files vanish — videos and photos must be re-downloaded
product.minus: An infuriating mechanic: already-downloaded media silently drops after days or weeks, so every time you open a chat the file must be fetched again. It burns mobile data, and saving videos to the gallery often fails.

product.title: The video player crops the picture and lags after the update
product.minus: The built-in player has degraded: video plays with lag, part of the frame is hidden at the bottom, and the picture is blown up beyond the screen. Whole channels report their videos are nearly unwatchable on Android.

product.title: Spam, scammers and NSFW ads creep right into chats
product.minus: The platform is drowning in scams: fraudsters everywhere, indecent ads injected into chats, and anti-spam tools locked behind Premium. Many warn that if you're not careful, it's easy to get scammed.

product.title: Channels, bots and folders make Telegram a powerhouse for work and communities
product.plus: What pros value: channels and bots for organizing communities, folders to tidy chats, and solid admin tools for massive groups. It works for work, school and business alike.

product.title: Arbitrary bans and a broken report system hit the innocent
product.minus: Moderation swings blindly: bans for stickers or a mere "accusation" of spam, with appeals ignored. Meanwhile the report system is trivially gamed — a crowd mass-reports an innocent user and they get restricted, while real abuse stays.

product.title: Endless "connecting" and freezes on the phone-number screen
product.minus: Basic stability wobbles: the app hangs on "connecting", spins forever after you enter your number, drops its connection on its own, or freezes on the contacts-permission prompt. For some it simply won't start.

product.title: Regional discrimination: harsh limits for Iran and country-based charges
product.minus: Rules differ by country and it lands as unfair: Iranians get their stories capped and can't log in without a VPN, while Africa and the developing world face a sudden paywall to sign in. Users flatly call it discrimination.

product.title: Privacy and zero ads are the core reason people love Signal
product.plus: Users switch from WhatsApp specifically for end-to-end encryption, open source code and the nonprofit model: no ads, no tracking, no data harvesting.

product.title: Switching to a new phone wipes your entire chat history
product.minus: Changing device or re-registering routinely ends in losing all chats and contacts: the code reads as "incorrect", the account gets "screwed up", and restoring old history across devices simply isn't possible.

product.title: Notifications arrive late or never arrive at all
product.minus: A recurring complaint: messages don't arrive until you manually open the app, and call/message notifications stay silent even with background permissions granted.

product.title: The "verify you are human" captcha loops forever
product.minus: During sign-up the captcha gets stuck in a loop: you solve the puzzle over and over with no progress, the verification code never arrives, and registration becomes impossible.

product.title: Linking a second device or desktop barely works
product.minus: You can't link an Android phone to an Android tablet, the desktop QR code never loads, and with more than one device message-sending gets blocked entirely.

product.title: The mandatory phone number alienates privacy-minded users
product.minus: The privacy-messenger paradox: just to chat you're forced to hand over a phone number even though people would gladly give an email, and kids without a number can't register at all.

product.title: Calls are crisp but drop on incoming cellular calls and weak network
product.minus: The audio gets praise, but a Signal call cuts off the moment a regular cellular call comes in (WhatsApp puts it on hold instead), and video freezes with voice breaking up on weak connections.

product.title: Scammers begging for gift cards have crept in here too
product.minus: Despite the privacy, users report scammers: contacts beg for gift cards and pose as celebrities — the same privacy that shields users also shields the fraudsters.

product.title: The clean, simple interface wins over users tired of bloated WhatsApp
product.plus: Many praise the minimalism on purpose: nothing extra, no stories or statuses, easy and light — "so boring and efficient. I love it".

product.title: Missing the familiar small stuff: last seen, stickers, statuses
product.minus: Users keep asking for features from Telegram, WhatsApp and Kakao: last seen, music posts, better gifs and stickers, link previews, scheduled messages on desktop.

product.title: Collapsed messages and "read more" annoy in everyday chatting
product.minus: Small but sharp UX gripes: long messages auto-collapse under "read more" with no way to disable it, forwarding order is broken, and the red dot on the floating bubble is hard to read.

product.title: Slow video and photo sending, sometimes stuck on compression
product.minus: Sending video drags on forever or never goes through, HD quality suffers, and in the evenings media gets stuck showing "compression".

product.title: Free international calls and messages are genuine value
product.plus: For families spread across countries, Signal is a way to talk with no international charges: calls to a son in England, friends abroad, relatives without roaming fees.

product.title: Endless "session expired" loop when switching accounts
product.minus: The app logs people out on its own — especially when switching between two accounts — and then won't let them back in: entering login and password just loops back to the same "Session expired, please log in again" message, the screen stops reacting to taps, and it drags on for days.

product.title: Accounts get disabled with no violation and no real review
product.minus: People report en masse that their account was disabled "for no reason", with no rule broken, and the appeal goes nowhere: memories, photos and ties to loved ones get locked away, and support doesn't help.

product.title: App hangs on the loading screen and pops a "there's a bug" notice
product.minus: A very common pattern: the app opens but spins an endless loading circle and never loads chats, then after a minute shows a pop-up about a bug. Clearing cache, reinstalling and updating help for a day or two, then it returns — while friends on the same phones have no issue.

product.title: Forced "confirm your identity" cuts people off from chatting
product.minus: After changing device or some "unusual activity", the app demands an identity check — a video selfie or passport/ID — and blocks messaging until then. The selfie "fails to upload", minors simply don't have the requested documents, and the person is left cut off from family and friends.

product.title: Messages get stuck on "sending" or arrive late
product.minus: Even on stable Wi-Fi messages hang on "sending" and never go through, sometimes vanishing entirely; notifications arrive late or not at all. Sometimes you can send but never receive the reply.

product.title: Frequent crashes and freezes, especially when switching profiles
product.minus: The app crashes every other time you open a chat or bubble and freezes solid when switching between personal and business profiles — even on powerful recent phones like the S22 Ultra after a clean reinstall and with plenty of free storage.

product.title: Forced PIN lock on your own chats annoys people
product.minus: People are irritated that accessing their own messages on their own phone now requires a PIN that seems forced on them.

product.title: Text box vanishes in Marketplace chats — no way to reply to buyers
product.minus: Sellers can't reply to buyers on Facebook Marketplace: the chat won't open or the text box disappears mid-typing, so you can't even see what you're writing — leaving only one canned reply.

product.title: Stripped-down features: games, chat heads and Notes gone
product.minus: Long-time users recall when you could play games, run polls and organize events, and "chat heads" bubbles opened straight from the screen. Now games are gone, bubbles are boxy and clunky, and Notes appear for some accounts but not others — the app feels hollowed out.

product.title: Blocking still sends notifications — a failure for harassment victims
product.minus: Even after blocking, deleting chats, leaving conversations and deactivating the profile, the app still sends notifications when the blocked person tries to make contact — defeating the whole point of blocking for people escaping stalkers and abuse.

product.title: Video and voice calls keep families connected across borders
product.plus: Despite all the bugs, the core value holds: people praise the crisp sound and good video quality on calls, the reliable connection, and being able to see and hear family and friends abroad for free — for many it's their only means of communication.

product.title: A simple, familiar way to message Facebook friends
product.plus: For those who stay, the app wins on being simple and familiar: an easy, intuitive interface, fast messaging, and a handy way to chat with family and Facebook friends right inside one ecosystem.

product.title: Forced ChatGPT that can't be removed
product.minus: A recent update bolted a ChatGPT thread on top of the chat list that can't be muted, deleted or hidden. There's a «Disconnect ChatGPT» option in settings, but it just throws «something went wrong» every single time. Users read it as AI forced on them that nobody asked for.

product.title: Number activation that fails for weeks
product.minus: The activation call never arrives, arrives late, or hangs up without giving a code; entering the last 4 digits returns «incorrect». There's no SMS fallback and attempts are capped once a day, so registration drags on for days and weeks — including for people who need Viber for work.

product.title: Accounts blocked with no reason as «spam»
product.minus: Long-time users get flagged as spammers and blocked for no reason, including work and school numbers. Recovery is only via a ticket and a 3-day wait, support often never replies, and the app you'd need to appeal through is itself locked.

product.title: Ads spill outside the app — over the dialer
product.minus: After you hang up an ordinary call, Viber drops an ad overlay onto the system dialer and pushes you to Shopee, Lazada, even casino sites. Ads show up in the chat list, in settings and when answering calls — banners an older person could mistake for the system itself.

product.title: Notifications arrive hours late or not at all
product.minus: Messages and calls land hours or even a day later, or with no notification at all, forcing users to open the app by hand. Sometimes it fires fake notifications about group messages that don't exist.

product.title: The core — message delivery — became unreliable
product.minus: Messages and photos hang on loading, send with lag, or never show up in history even though the sender's screenshot proves they were sent. Some have to reboot the phone after every message. The one core job of a messenger works worse than rivals.

product.title: Forced redesign with no way back to old colors
product.minus: An update turned messages bright purple, dimmed the background and killed the calm grey bubbles and old themes (sand, forest, purple stars). There's no option to revert — and for light-sensitive users the screaming contrast is exhausting on the eyes.

product.title: Support practically doesn't exist
product.minus: There's no in-app support — you're routed through tedious website steps where the chatbot is broken and email replies are templated and ignore the actual issue. Tickets sit for days and weeks with no response, and the promised «within 24 hours» reply never comes.

product.title: Switching phones loses your chat history
product.minus: QR chat transfer doesn't work — after scanning it shows some JSON and stalls, and backup throws «Error». Between Android and iPhone the backup won't migrate at all, and people lose years of history when they change devices.

product.title: Bloated into a bazaar: dating, payments, wallet, business chats
product.minus: The messenger is stuffed with dating, a marketplace, a wallet and payments that can't be turned off, plus it yanks you from a chat into Viber Dating, and ads pop up on holiday keywords. Business chats can no longer be opted out of by default. Users beg for a lite version — they only want messaging.

product.title: Spam and scams Viber itself won't filter
product.minus: Two or three scammers slide into DMs every day, and spam messages can't be deleted, blocked or reported via long-press. Meanwhile the app ships with 21 trackers and weak privacy — anyone with your phone number can find your profile.

product.title: A regional anchor people have loved for years
product.plus: For families and businesses across Eastern Europe, Ukraine and Myanmar, Viber is the default: people have used it for years and praise its simplicity, free calls and video, and stickers. A chunk of users still call it fast, reliable and a favorite «for a decade».

product.title: The go-to place to hang out with friends and communities
product.plus: The core thing people love is how easily it lets them chat, call and game together, make friends around shared interests, and stay in touch even when people change phone numbers.

product.title: You can connect without a phone number, just an email
product.plus: Many value being able to add and call friends by email rather than a phone number — that's exactly why people picked Discord over call apps like Snapchat.

product.title: Voice just drops in calls, especially when sharing screen
product.minus: The most widespread pain: people can't hear each other in calls, screen-share has no audio, and on mobile you join voice already muted while soundless screen-sharing has become the norm.

product.title: Calls keep dropping and kicking you out of voice
product.minus: Beyond audio, calls regularly drop, reconnect, or kick you out of group chat on their own — sometimes the call ends by itself even when you're doing nothing.

product.title: The "are you a robot" captcha hard-blocks signup and login
product.minus: The bot check is its own hell: after pressing confirm the app crashes or shows a blank screen, people can't create an account for a month, and end up deleting the app.

product.title: Logging into your own account is a lottery: password, OTP, MFA, passkey
product.minus: Login is a constant source of despair: a correct password is rejected, OTPs never arrive, QR login now demands a password anyway, and you can't make a passkey without the very password you forgot.

product.title: Images, videos and files stubbornly won't send or download
product.minus: Sending media on mobile is broken: images take five tries, files won't send even after a reinstall, media only downloads via the browser, and the free limit was cut to 15MB.

product.title: The new minimalist UI killed phone navigation
product.minus: The recent redesign reads as aesthetics over function: mentions and the friends list are now a hassle to find, the bottom has a fat profile bar instead of buttons, and familiar navigation was dropped for looks.

product.title: Crashes, freezes and lag — in an app nearly a decade old
product.minus: Basic stability is shaky: the app crashes, freezes, stops opening after updates, and runs heavy even on decent phones — and per users, it goes unfixed for years.

product.title: Notifications don't arrive or pile into one heap
product.minus: Despite notifications being on and reinstalls done, they simply don't arrive on the phone for years — and when they do, they're all bundled together regardless of server, including DMs.

product.title: Nitro is shoved in your face while basic quality sits behind a paywall
product.minus: Monetization grates: pop-up Nitro offers, an "ads everywhere" feeling, and decent image quality, video size and proper screen-share now locked behind a paid subscription.

product.title: AI moderation bans without explanation, and support stonewalls
product.minus: The most painful thread is unfair bans and limits from an AI bot: no reason given, vague "you violated the Terms" with no specifics, appeals denied, and human support is effectively unreachable.

product.title: Accounts get hijacked, and support won't help recover them
product.minus: A worrying security theme: people get hacked repeatedly, hackers set their own 2FA, scammers pose as admins and "staff", and support won't help recover the account or even charged-back money.

product.title: Mandatory age and ID verification drives people to seek alternatives
product.minus: The new demand to confirm age and hand an ID to a third-party site triggers outright refusal: people remove Discord, try to move friends to other platforms, and look for a service not hosted on US soil.

product.title: Sign-up forces another 6-month user to scan a QR code for you
product.minus: To finish signing up you need a friend who's been on WeChat for 6 months to scan a QR code on your screen. If you know nobody on the app, registration is literally impossible.

product.title: The SMS / voice verification code never arrives
product.minus: People with good signal and balance wait hours for an SMS or call code that never comes, while the app blames an "unstable network" — even though SMS from everyone else arrives fine.

product.title: Accounts get locked without warning and are near-impossible to recover
product.minus: The app abruptly blocks accounts for "suspicious activity" or "spam" — even for people who added a couple of acquaintances. Unlocking drags on for days or weeks, and support often goes silent.

product.title: Switching phones means losing your account and all contacts
product.minus: Moving to a new phone requires a QR code the old phone must scan — but the old phone logs itself out in the process. People permanently lose the contacts they made in China.

product.title: The app downloads an outdated version, then says it's outdated
product.minus: Right after installing from the store, the app complains the version is outdated and pushes you to a sketchy website for an apk that won't install. On Android 14 it downloads version 7.0.

product.title: Devours storage and battery even when idle
product.minus: The app balloons to gigabytes right after registration, keeps all media in internal storage with no fine-grained control, and drains the battery even when you never open it.

product.title: Feels like it only works for Chinese phone numbers
product.minus: Users in the US, UK, Russia and elsewhere struggle for hours and days, concluding the app effectively isn't meant for anyone outside China.

product.title: Too many verification layers — face, ID, bank card
product.minus: On top of SMS, the app demands a selfie, passport or ID photo, and a bank card — yet the photo upload fails anyway. Many feel it's just harvesting personal data.

product.title: Password recovery is an interrogation you can't pass
product.minus: Resetting a password means answering a dozen questions near-perfectly; after a few misses you're locked out for days, sometimes forced to wait 7 days before trying again.

product.title: The indispensable all-in-one super app for dealing with China
product.plus: Chat, voice and video calls, WeChat Pay, Moments and mini-programs — one app replacing a dozen others. For business and connecting with China, users call it a non-negotiable must-have.

product.title: Built-in translation bridges the language barrier
product.plus: Users single out the built-in message and camera translation as accurate and genuinely helpful for talking with Chinese friends and travelling in China.

product.title: Clear calls and smooth media sharing
product.plus: Those who get past sign-up praise the crisp voice and video calls, fast photo and video sharing, and smooth group chats even on Android.

product.title: Missing basic messenger features like read receipts and online status
product.minus: Even happy users note WeChat lags behind: no delivered/read receipts, no online status, no message editing — features WhatsApp and Viber already have.

product.title: Ads inside the settings menu that can't be hidden
product.minus: A "Stores and Cards" entry and ads are baked into the "Me" menu with no way to hide them, sharing one red dot with real settings notices to lure you into tapping.

product.title: Killing phone-number login locks people out of old accounts
product.minus: LINE abruptly disabled phone-number login everywhere except a few Asian countries. Users whose accounts aren't linked to Google, Apple or email are completely locked out — no access to years of chats, contacts and purchased stickers.

product.title: Account transfer is impossible without the old device
product.minus: To sign in on a new phone, LINE demands confirmation from the old device — a QR code or a code sent in chat. But if the old phone is broken, lost or wiped, there's nowhere to get the code, and the account becomes inaccessible.

product.title: Paid stickers and themes make chats more expressive
product.plus: A huge collection of branded stickers, emoji and themes is what people love LINE for. Many call them the cutest and most varied of any messenger, and stickers are what make chatting feel alive.

product.title: Unsending your own messages got locked behind Premium
product.minus: Unsending a message after the one-hour window is now only available with the paid LINE Premium plan. Users see it as extortion: a basic feature that used to be free, walled off behind a paywall.

product.title: A forced in-chat AI agent you can't turn off
product.minus: An AI agent was added to chats — it takes up screen space and can't be disabled permanently, only "hidden" for 30 days. Users also flag the lack of consent: if the person you're talking to uses the AI, your data gets fed into it.

product.title: Accounts get banned with no reason given
product.minus: Freshly created accounts get suspended out of nowhere, sometimes before sending a single message. Support refuses to name a reason, citing "terms of service", and there's no way to get the account reactivated.

product.title: Chats take 10-60 seconds to load every single time
product.minus: After recent updates the app stopped being an instant messenger: the chat list takes tens of seconds to load and each individual conversation opens with another delay — every single time. Notifications arrive 20+ minutes late.

product.title: Support doesn't respond, or responds with a bot
product.minus: There's no help section, no chat or phone line, and the contact form just opens the very app the user can't log into. Replies take weeks and come only from a bot — no real humans to be found.

product.title: Crystal-clear voice and video across distances
product.plus: When login works, LINE remains a reliable way to stay in touch with friends and family abroad: voice and video calls are praised as crystal clear even over long distances.

product.title: Region locks cut off users around the world
product.minus: LINE is pushed worldwide, yet outside Japan region restrictions keep piling up: you can't register a UK, Bangladesh or Romania number, can't add friends overseas, can't connect between Hong Kong and Taiwan.

product.title: Finding and adding friends often just fails
product.minus: Adding a friend means digging through hidden settings to enable your LINE ID, only to hit "ID not found", a tries limit, or a region block. You can't search by username, and People Nearby refreshes itself the moment you open a profile.

product.title: Backups and chat history are lost for good
product.minus: Full chat backup and restore are premium-only and limited to some countries, history is capped at 100MB per account, and media isn't saved to Google Drive. On a new device users find empty chats stripped of old messages, photos and voice notes.

product.title: Filters and lenses are the core reason people love the app
product.plus: Creative filters, lenses and effects are what people open Snapchat for: they shoot fun photos and videos, share moments and just play around to lift their mood.

product.title: Easy chatting with friends and family keeps people in the app
product.plus: For many the real value is a simple way to chat, call and share everyday snaps with close people and online friends, even across Android and iPhone.

product.title: Memories pushed behind a paywall — storage suddenly costs money
product.minus: Snapchat cut free memories storage and now forces a monthly plan for what was free for years; for people who kept their photo archive here since 2022 it feels like paying ransom for their own pictures.

product.title: The camera breaks on calls and photos: black screen, pixelation, won't capture
product.minus: The core feature — the camera — simply fails for many: a black screen with filters, pixelated and frozen video on calls, and 'cannot open camera' errors even after granting every permission.

product.title: Device and account bans with no explanation, and support that won't help
product.minus: Users get banned for no clear reason, lose thousands of followers, see several devices blocked at once (the SS06 error), and the support team simply ignores appeals and hacked accounts.

product.title: Notifications won't turn off: ads and lenses push through even when disabled
product.minus: People switch notifications off, yet the app still pushes ads, Team Snapchat messages and lens alerts, taking up a quarter of the screen and ignoring the settings.

product.title: Unsafe content: unsolicited explicit pictures, body-selling and minors
product.minus: Parents and ordinary users complain about a stream of inappropriate messages and pictures, sexting beggars and minors selling themselves; blocking doesn't help and moderation feels absent.

product.title: The 'Add to Story' button sits too close to 'Save' — private clips end up public
product.minus: Because the 'Add to Story' button sits right next to send and save, people accidentally post private videos to their whole Story and can't delete them in time — users beg for at least a confirmation pop-up.

product.title: A forced public profile and the algorithm buried ordinary creators' content
product.minus: Snapchat added a public profile nobody asked for: every story goes public and Spotlight stopped giving views — creators feel their content is buried by the algorithm.

product.title: Streaks and friend location are the addictive hook that pulls people back daily
product.plus: Streaks with friends and the friend-location map have become a habit: people come back every day to keep the streak alive and see where friends are, which drives engagement better than most features.

product.title: Streaks reset due to glitches, and there's no free restore
product.minus: The very thing that hooks people — streaks — also lets them down: streaks vanish because of app glitches, can't be restored, and users waste money on paid restores that don't work.

product.title: Laggy, freezing, and hangs the whole phone, especially after updates
product.minus: The app lags, stutters and crashes, drains the battery, and for some it hangs the entire phone after install — frequent updates bring new bugs instead of stability.

product.title: Removed 'Clear All Chats' — conversations must be cleared one by one
product.minus: Snapchat removed the option to clear all chats at once, including AI and Team Snapchat chats, so conversations now have to be deleted one by one — a small but irritating regression.

product.title: Log out once and you're locked out for good
product.minus: The single most common pain: after logging out or switching phones, sign-in simply stops working — the app demands a "latest version" that doesn't exist in the store, or repeats "something went wrong, try again later" for weeks on end.

product.title: Creating an account is physically impossible
product.minus: Sign-up is flat-out broken: on the "join" screen the username field won't tap or accept text (while the password field works fine), or it throws an endless update error. Whole friend groups of 17 fail to register at once.

product.title: Ads literally break the app
product.minus: The ads aren't just annoying — they're aggressive and inescapable: pop-ups with no close button, forced redirects to the store, and for some the ads freeze the phone until restart. "8 ads every 10 minutes."

product.title: Messages get stuck on "S" and never arrive
product.minus: The core job of a messenger fails: messages hang on the "S" status for days, arrive hours late, or never arrive at all. Some users see over half their messages never send.

product.title: Bots and scammers have taken over
product.minus: The defining social rot: feeds and DMs are swamped with bots, fakes and scammers begging for money and gift cards. Blocking is useless — a spam-bot spins up new usernames in minutes and finds you again.

product.title: A ban-bot punishes the innocent for decades
product.minus: Moderation is handed to an AI that bans for nothing — for terms running to the year 2092–2093, on one disgruntled person's report, while appeals with proof are ignored. Meanwhile the actual offenders stay free.

product.title: Notifications for messages that don't exist
product.minus: Notifications work backwards: pushes fire when there are no messages (often disguised ads or premium promos), while real messages only show once you open the app. Instead of the text you get a faceless "New Kik message".

product.title: You can't change your photo or profile banner
product.minus: The most basic profile setting has been broken for months: the avatar and banner won't change on either old or new accounts, and messages from contacts stop arriving. Basics that worked for years simply fell off.

product.title: Play Integrity locks honest users out of a chat app
product.minus: A sudden Play Integrity check at login throws a "device has failed to play integrity checks" error and blocks devices that don't need it — users rightly ask why a chat app demands such checks at all.

product.title: It used to be brilliantly simple — and that's still loved
product.plus: Beneath all the rage runs genuine nostalgia: people remember Kik as a reliable, simple messenger that let you meet and chat without a phone number, with chat history stored locally rather than in the cloud. Many keep it for years just for old contacts.

product.title: The platform has become unsafe for people
product.minus: A heavy reputational pain: users widely report predators, child exploitation, cyberbullying and harassment — and complain that reports are ignored while offenders' accounts stay live. Some get banned precisely for reporting such behavior.

product.title: There's no support — just an AI stand-in
product.minus: When things break there's nowhere to turn: the "Help Center" is an AI looping the same useless advice, review replies are bot-written too, and the links in them don't work. Support emails go unresolved.

product.title: Lag, overheating and constant crashes
product.minus: Performance has rotted: the app lags and glitches, kicks you out, closes the keyboard mid-typing, overheats the phone and bloats with gigabytes of data that need constant cache-clearing.

product.title: A paid premium pushed on top of a broken app
product.minus: While login is broken and ads pile up, Kik aggressively sells a beta premium: fake notifications turn out to be subscription promos, and some users are only let in after paying. Charging for a beta of a broken product feels like a slap.

product.title: Forced Alexa/Rufus AI hijacks search with no way to disable it
product.minus: By far the loudest complaint: a normal search opens an AI page that restates what you typed and pushes sponsored items instead of showing products. To get real results you wait for it to load and press a separate button, and there's no off switch even though Amazon claims there is.

product.title: AI and a heavy update made the app slow, freezing and crashing
product.minus: Even on flagship phones search takes "forever", pages sit blank for minutes, and the app freezes or crashes. Many tie it directly to the added AI, which they say eats resources and bandwidth.

product.title: Prime promises 1-2 day delivery, but packages show up late
product.minus: People pay for Prime for guaranteed fast shipping, yet dates keep slipping: the promised date changes after you've paid, "next day" becomes a week, and a refund only comes if it's more than a week late.

product.title: Support is AI bots and dead-end links; you can't reach a human
product.minus: Reaching a real agent is nearly impossible: the AI chat leads to dead-end links, refund promises go unfulfilled, and agents stall the chat until it closes. Some say support isn't even an option until an order is marked delivered.

product.title: Orders get auto-cancelled, and refunds are slow or never come
product.minus: Orders cancel themselves for no reason, sometimes repeatedly, and money gets stuck: one person lost $200 with no refund, others wait 7 days or are refused outright. Uploading an ID with a promised "3-day fix" drags on for weeks.

product.title: Login, verification and account recovery have become a maze
product.minus: The app logs you out constantly, verification wipes your progress when adding an account, demands an old phone number you no longer have, and makes you wait 24 hours after filling out forms. Some would rather pay competitors because giving Amazon money got too hard.

product.title: The app dropped support for tablets and older Android
product.minus: People who shop from a tablet or older device got cut off: the app is "no longer available" for their tablet, only installs on other devices, and stops working on Android 11/12/14. They refuse to upgrade hardware just for this.

product.title: Product and review feeds are sliding toward Temu-style junk and fakes
product.minus: Search surfaces dropship brands and "Temu junk" at inflated prices, reviews are botted, and the new version shows only 10 reviews per product — mostly 5-star — which users see as a push toward impulse buying.

product.title: Core UX strips familiar features: price filter, dark mode, screenshots
product.minus: Small things that break the routine: price filtering removed, still no dark mode (when every rival has one), you can't screenshot without a "share" pop-up, and the orders list is a mess with no way to mark something received.

product.title: Unmatched selection: finds what local stores don't have
product.plus: The main reason people stay: Amazon has the rare and locally-unavailable — manga, G7 LPS figures, books in a small town, things not even stocked in big states. For many it's the irreplaceable everything-store.

product.title: A lifeline for people who can't easily get out
product.plus: For elderly, disabled and busy people, delivery to the door is a genuine lifeline: they can get everything they need without leaving home. Many call it indispensable and thank Amazon for their quality of life.

product.title: When it works, returns and Prime delivery are painless
product.plus: For satisfied users the experience is smooth: free, hassle-free returns, reliable two-day Prime delivery, and the right item to the right address. To them Amazon is still the "gold standard" of online retail.

product.title: Applying a search filter hangs the app forever on "Searching"
product.minus: The single most common complaint: the moment you add or change a search filter, the screen freezes on "Searching" with a blank page and never loads. Reinstalling, clearing cache and restarting do nothing, and people miss auctions because of it.

product.title: Forced Live shopping turns the feed into "TikTok for scalpers"
product.minus: eBay Live has taken over the home screen and search with autoplaying videos that can't be turned off. Users call it trashy slop, "OnlyFans for Pokemon scammers", and overwhelmingly demand an off switch — otherwise they bail to the website or to competitors.

product.title: Fees swallow nearly half of the seller's payout
product.minus: Sellers are stunned by the cut: a $76 sale nets $62, a $40 sale nets $6.75, on top of a new Buyer Protection fee, paid "promotion", and inflated eBay shipping. The "free to sell" ads feel like a lie, pushing people to Vinted, Mercari and Marketplace.

product.title: AI is force-fed into both listing and support
product.minus: Listings now must go through an AI assistant with no off switch — it misreads the item and writes nonsense you have to erase and retype. Support has collapsed into a chatbot that loops endlessly and offers no path to a real human.

product.title: A login loop: "Invalid access token" logs you out and won't let you back
product.minus: After updates the app randomly logs people out and on sign-in throws "Invalid access token. Check the value of the Authorisation HTTP request header", demanding a full data wipe or password reset. Sellers miss messages and sales because of it.

product.title: Seller funds are held for a week-plus after delivery
product.minus: eBay holds payouts even after a completed, delivered sale, demanding driver's license, birth certificate and other documents. People report going weeks "not paid for anything" with funds blocked and no explanation.

product.title: Buyer and seller protection doesn't actually work against scams
product.minus: Both buyers and sellers describe AI closing their cases with absurd verdicts, the money-back guarantee turning out to be "a marketing trick", and used-item returns screwing the seller. The reviews are full of "AVOID" and talk of a class-action lawsuit.

product.title: Spam notifications and emails that can't be switched off
product.minus: Push alerts about eBay Live arrive hourly, sometimes twice an hour, plus 14 emails per single purchase and notifications at 12:20 a.m. There's no setting to stop them, so the only fix is banning notifications entirely — which kills real sale alerts too.

product.title: Last-second auction sniping: shown as top bidder, then outbid
product.minus: eBay's beloved auction feature is undermined: the app shows you as top bidder the whole countdown, then in the last 2 seconds you're outbid with no chance to respond and no losing notification. Users ask for a clock reset like eBay Live already has.

product.title: An enormous catalog: "find anything you could ever want"
product.plus: The core reason long-timers stay: eBay genuinely has everything — childhood retro games, stamps, cards, car parts, surgical instruments, items you can't find anywhere else. It's a one-of-a-kind resale market where you compare price and quality in one place.

product.title: Selling from the phone beats the PC: snap a photo and it's listed
product.plus: Sellers love the mobility: no more transferring photos from a computer — point, shoot, and the item is in the listing. You can run a whole shop from the app with no PC, and Seller Hub gives data insights and fast payouts.

product.title: Inflated, inflexible shipping through eBay's forced postage system
product.minus: The new system forces you to buy postage only through eBay — pricier, less flexible, with no option to ship it yourself. The weight auto-estimate is wrong and real shipping costs spike so badly sellers lose money: a $53 grill costing $83 to ship.

product.title: General instability: crashes, "network error" and lag
product.minus: Beyond search, the app falls over generally: constant "network error" and "server unavailable", white screens, freezes, slow loading and crashes after weekly updates. Some users report it suddenly became incompatible with their device entirely.

product.title: For loyal users, losing it would be "like losing a limb"
product.plus: Despite all the negativity, there's a solid core of 20-25-year veterans for whom eBay is irreplaceable: they check it first before any purchase, trust it with cards and collections, and say life without it would be poorer. It's a familiar, convenient tool that "just works" for them.

product.title: The app freezes and crashes right at checkout
product.minus: The single most common complaint: the app locks up, closes itself and drops connection exactly at checkout, forcing a fresh start and often losing the reserved delivery slot.

product.title: The card gets declined right at the final payment step
product.minus: A full cart and chosen slot get killed by a "card not accepted" message — even though the bank confirms the problem isn't on their end; switching and saving cards also keep failing.

product.title: A lifeline for disabled and elderly shoppers
product.plus: The warmest praise: door delivery for people recovering from surgery, with disabilities, without a car, or in nursing homes — literally what spares them an exhausting trip to the store.

product.title: You pay for Walmart+ and still get hit with a fee for orders under $35
product.minus: Subscribers are furious that after paying for the membership they're still charged $6.99 on orders under $35 — and the fee only appears after the order is submitted, which feels like a bait-and-switch.

product.title: They removed the shipping option — now everything is delivery only
product.minus: An update removed the ship and in-store pickup options: even items that can only be shipped get labeled as delivery, and the app itself can't tell what's actually available in the store.

product.title: The app no longer shows where an item is located in the store
product.minus: It used to show the aisle and in-store availability; now the app hides that, pushes delivery, and even when you search "in store now" won't let you buy without shipping.

product.title: Relentless Walmart+ upsells and a flood of in-app ads
product.minus: Shoppers are worn down by the membership pitch nearly every time they open the app and dozens of pop-ups at checkout, plus in-app ads that get in the way of simply placing an order.

product.title: Money is taken instantly, but refunds drag on and you have to fight for them
product.minus: Cancellations and order errors turn into 7–10-day-plus holds; getting money back means disputing with the bank or chasing it yourself, especially painful for baby formula and prescription orders.

product.title: Deliveries arrive wrong, incomplete, late, or at the wrong address entirely
product.minus: Late windows, missing items with no price adjustment, other people's orders, and drop-offs at the wrong address — drivers swap items without approval and don't notify when an order is delivered.

product.title: EBT and gift cards work intermittently and break the order
product.minus: The EBT balance check was removed, EBT won't cover eligible items and demands cash on top, and redeeming gift cards reliably rejects the order.

product.title: When it works — convenient, cheap, and faster than Amazon
product.plus: The core strength: easy ordering, free and often same-day delivery, competitive prices and a broad selection — many say outright they're switching from Amazon to Walmart.

product.title: Privacy concerns: data handed to third parties without consent
product.minus: Users accuse the app of harvesting data while ignoring privacy requests, complain about a foisted OnePay wallet handed their cards and contacts, and a 45-day data-deletion wait.

product.title: "Free gifts" that you have to pay for
product.minus: The number-one complaint: the app promises free gifts or a prize, then at the end demands you buy $10–20 more or invite friends. People feel cheated — the reward never actually arrives.

product.title: Gamification that feels like a casino
product.minus: Spinning wheels, "wins," and scarcity counters ("only 2 left") read as casino mechanics designed to make you buy. Many call it manipulative and predatory.

product.title: Botched orders: wrong item or nothing at all
product.minus: A common pain: they ship the wrong item (women's shirts instead of men's, the wrong knife) or part of the order simply "disappears," and the refund has to be fought for.

product.title: Not as pictured: size and quality lie
product.minus: Photos mislead on size (a "36-inch" bag turns out to be 10) and clothes are a cheap version of the picture, running 1–2 sizes small. "Cheap does not mean good."

product.title: Forced minimum-cart threshold
product.minus: To check out or get free shipping you must hit a $15–30 cart minimum. It frustrates people who want one small thing but are forced to pad the order.

product.title: Bombardment of notifications and ads
product.minus: A flood of push notifications, emails, and intrusive ads across other platforms. People compare it to being stalked — "more harassment than my ex."

product.title: Cluttered UI and motion overload
product.minus: The screen is packed with animations and moving images — the payment button gets lost, some users literally get motion sickness, and pop-up "rewards" are impossible to dismiss.

product.title: Slow, unreliable delivery
product.minus: Couriers are the weak link: parcels get lost, returned to the warehouse, or sit "arrived in country" for weeks without delivery. For many the order never came at all, even after months.

product.title: Low product quality
product.minus: A share of buyers complain about junk that breaks on day one, gadgets that don't work (watches that lie about steps and heart rate), and clothes they can't wear.

product.title: Price and selection — the real reason people come back
product.plus: Despite all the gripes, the happy core praises the huge selection at rock-bottom prices: you can fill a suitcase for less than three brand-name T-shirts, and some items genuinely exceed expectations.

product.title: Returns and refunds work when something goes wrong
