product.plus: The team replies fast to emails and comments — many bump their review from 2-3 to 5 stars right after a support exchange; for some that's the deciding plus, though others are annoyed by email-only help with no in-app answers.

product.title: «Free» turns out to be a trial that flips to a subscription
product.minus: People install it believing it's free, spend time entering data and signing up, then hit an $79.99/year or $17–20/month paywall. The irony stings: an app that promises to get you out of debt asks you to add one more bill.

product.title: After an update you simply can't sign in — it hangs on the login screen
product.minus: The single most common technical complaint: an update breaks login. Buttons press but do nothing, the screen hangs grey, the app bounces you to a webpage that never loads. Reinstalling, password resets and cache clears don't help, and years of data become unreachable.

product.title: You have to sort every single transaction by hand
product.minus: By design the app categorizes nothing automatically — you drag every purchase into its line and re-set the budget from scratch each month. For some that manual friction is deliberate «accountability»; for others it's tedious busywork that sends them back to Excel.

product.title: Bank sync lags for days and spawns duplicate transactions
product.minus: Even on premium, transactions import 2–4 days late, you must constantly reconnect the bank, and a single purchase sometimes duplicates two to four times. To know your balance you end up opening your bank app anyway — defeating the whole «real-time budget» promise.

product.title: Every update makes the app worse and more bloated
product.minus: Long-time users say it in one voice: the app used to be great, then updates removed handy features, hid them behind premium, and piled on an intrusive home screen, pop-ups, «lessons» and ads. A budgeting tool is being turned into an everything-app.

product.title: Charges land suddenly and without warning
product.minus: People get billed immediately instead of after the promised 7 days, are charged $79.99 after cancelling, and get no heads-up email before annual renewal. For a debt-strapped audience, a surprise $80 hit feels like a blow from the very people preaching thrift.

product.title: The budget assumes you know your income upfront — irregular pay breaks it
product.minus: The method is built on a projected monthly income, so with unstable or weekly pay the app still shows the full projected amount as available to spend. For variable earners, working out the real balance is nearly impossible — Excel ends up more flexible.

product.title: The math doesn't add up: the remaining balance is wrong
product.minus: Users catch the app in plain arithmetic errors: «remaining to spend» doesn't match what's actually left, a category turns red as overspent when it isn't, and plan/spent/remaining figures simply don't reconcile. For a budgeting app, broken math undermines the one thing it must get right.

product.title: The «every dollar a job» method actually changes habits and clears debt
product.plus: The headline praise: the zero-based approach forces you to name a purpose for every dollar, users finally see where money leaks, find hundreds of dollars of «margin» and genuinely pay down debt. Many say it changed how their household handles money.

product.title: The paycheck planner shows how much money you'll have on any day of the month
product.plus: A favorite among regulars: the paycheck planner spreads income and expenses across dates and shows how much you should have on any given day. It removes the manual «will I make it to next payday» math and makes cash flow predictable.

product.title: Shared budgeting gets spouses onto the same financial page
product.plus: Couples single out the shared access: both partners see the budget, the numbers «don't lie», and for the first time they can agree on spending without fights. For many it's less an accounting tool than a marriage-communication one.

product.title: The free version works for manual tracking, and premium pays for itself via auto-import
product.plus: Despite paywall complaints, a chunk of users are happy: the free tier is enough for manual budgeting if you log in daily, and premium's automatic bank import saves time and, they say, pays for itself in money saved within the first month.

product.title: The paywall greets you before the product does
product.minus: The subscription is demanded on the very first screen: you create an account and the «choose a plan» prompt is already there. You can't even add a second wallet, connect a bank, or look around without paying. Users compare it to paying the restaurant cover charge before seeing the menu.

product.title: The upsell hits even the people who already paid
product.minus: Every launch greets you with a full-screen «limited time» subscription promo — and even Premium and Lifetime users see it. The close (X) icon often doesn't respond to taps. People say outright they're considering switching purely because of this spam.

product.title: After the update the app opens on your very first transaction
product.minus: A fresh bug: on every launch the timeline jumps back to the earliest month (2015/2016/2021), so to log a new transaction you have to scroll through years of data. Many dropped their rating from 5 to 1-2 stars over exactly this: «it was perfect, now it's barely usable».

product.title: Bank connection simply never completes
product.minus: A pervasive bug: after authorizing at the bank (via Plaid or the bank site) the app dumps you back on the Spendee homepage and never applies the connection. People run the flow 3-4 times, hit a white screen or a broken deep-link redirect — and for a paid feature that's an immediate dealbreaker.

product.title: Degrading performance: slower year after year
product.minus: Since the «big update» the app turned sluggish: 7-second cold start, 20-30 seconds to add a transaction, lag even on flagship phones. Long-time users (since 2015) say they'd rather see optimization than «trendy» AI features. Support suggests a reinstall — and nothing else.

product.title: Local banks unsupported — useless outside a handful of countries
product.minus: The headline feature — bank sync — is dead for most markets: India, Mexico, Peru, Colombia, Malaysia, Vietnam, New Zealand, Somalia. Some places offer 3 banks, others just throw «error occurred». And you only find out after signing up and handing over your data.

product.title: The free trial turns into an instant charge
product.minus: The ad promises a 7-day free trial, but the card is charged immediately — with no way to exit the trial. Users demand refunds that aren't granted and call the scheme worthy of a store ban. Some report double charges and an annual fee with no warning.

product.title: Abandonment: years with no new features except «trendy» AI
product.minus: Users since 2014 feel the app is an abandoned project: long-promised small fixes never ship, widgets were removed 5 years ago and never restored, tablet mode was cut. Meanwhile a useless Magic AI Scan and an NFT feature appeared — and the scan even covers up the labels list.

product.title: Real-time cross-platform sync — the reason people stay
product.plus: The standout strength: one account works on Android, iOS, and the browser with data updating in real time across every device. It's web-based, not local storage, so your data isn't trapped on one phone — this is what users put up with everything else for.

product.title: Clean, beautiful, intuitive interface — the thing people love
product.plus: The design is consistently called one of the most beautiful among budget trackers: clean minimalist UI, excellent UX, colorful categories, and clear visualization of spending. For many it's the simplicity and pleasant look that make effortless tracking possible.

product.title: Support that actually fixes things — but often only after a public review
product.plus: When support engages, it often delivers: full refunds, a fixed build within a week, hands-on help with a local New Zealand bank. The catch — many only get a reply after leaving a public review, and some tickets sit unanswered for weeks.

product.title: Multi-currency wallets and budgets — for people living across borders
product.plus: Multi-currency support, shared wallets, and clear charts make Spendee handy for families, couples, and anyone spending across currencies. Custom categories and colored tags let people organize their tracking exactly the way they want.

product.title: Missing basics: split transactions, subcategories, a widget, and CSV import
product.minus: Even happy users list the gaps: you can't split one transaction across categories, there are no subcategories, no home-screen widget for quick entry, and no CSV import from a bank. Some leave for Wallet specifically over split transactions and a cheaper lifetime plan.

product.title: Credit cards and debts break the net-worth math
product.minus: Link a credit card or a loan and its balance adds to your net worth instead of subtracting, while card payments show up as income. There's no way to mark an account as «debt». For anyone who wants to see real free money, the tool simply doesn't work here.

product.title: Paywalled export holds your own data hostage
product.minus: Exporting your full history requires Premium, and even then it caps at 365 days — years of older data stay locked away. Users call it extortion and a GDPR violation; for some the export glitches out entirely. Leaving the app with your own records is hard.

product.title: Bank sync is the defining failure: it breaks after a few days and stays broken for months
product.minus: People buy premium specifically for bank auto-sync, yet it drops after 2-3 days, demands constant reauthorization, and sits unfixed for months — the core paid feature simply stops working.

product.title: You can't create top-level categories — only sub-sub-categories
product.minus: Everyone has a different spending structure, but the app forces its own bloated list and won't let you add a new category — only nest under an existing subcategory, which pushes many users to give up.

product.title: Support is effectively dead — even for premium customers
product.minus: A bot answers everything, users get ghosted after the first reply, acknowledged bugs go unfixed for months, and at times the ticket option was removed entirely — paying customers are left alone with broken features.

product.title: Bought premium, then discovered their bank isn't supported
product.minus: There's no clear warning about bank support before payment: users from India, Mexico, Vietnam, Kazakhstan and elsewhere pay for lifetime premium for sync, only to find their bank simply isn't on the list.

product.title: The best tracker for people who log everything manually
product.plus: Even with no bank sync at all, the app shines in manual mode: easy to enter and categorize spending and see the full picture across accounts — which is exactly why many love it for years.

product.title: Lifetime license instead of endless subscription — users love it
product.plus: The option to pay once for lifetime access instead of subscribing forever is a decisive plus for many and the reason they switched over from competitors like YNAB.

product.title: Records and entire accounts vanish; sync duplicates and deletes data
product.minus: Users lose data: transactions and whole accounts disappear, sync creates duplicates when shared, and deleting an account wipes its entire history — making it impossible to trust as a system of record.

product.title: Sudden logouts and data loss after forced sign-in
product.minus: The app increasingly logs people out on its own and then won't let them back in while their data appears gone; a forced mandatory sign-in on update also wiped the old records of offline users.

product.title: Clean, intuitive interface with clear visual charts
product.plus: A simple, pleasant interface with pie charts and graphs gives an instant view of spending by category — the single most praised thing on the positive side.

product.title: Intrusive premium ads on the home screen
product.minus: Constant pop-up upgrade banners annoy even paying users — to the point of getting notifications to upgrade a lifetime license to a lifetime license.

product.title: Bank sync demands you hand over your online banking login, password and OTP
product.minus: To import transactions the app asks for your net-banking username, password and OTP — which alarms many users who just want offline tracking without surrendering banking access.

product.title: Growing slowness, bugs and freezes, especially after updates
product.minus: Users say every update breaks something: the app lags, hangs, shows blank screens, search stops working — and bugs flagged years ago remain unfixed.

product.title: Billed for subscription even after uninstalling
product.minus: Some users report billing trouble: charged for months after uninstalling, paid premium never activated, and refund requests ignored.

product.title: Reliable cross-device sync of your own data plus web access
product.plus: Setting banks aside, syncing your own records across phone, tablet and the web version is praised as fast and reliable — a key plus for people working across several devices.

product.title: Clean, simple interface is the core reason for love and years of loyalty
product.plus: Users describe it in one word: simple, clean, no useless noise. Many have stayed 7-10 years precisely for the minimalism and clarity — you see where you stand financially without overload.

product.title: Ads pop up at the exact moment of entering an amount — breaking quick logging
product.minus: Ads appear precisely when someone is trying to quickly log a transaction, which makes the app useless in real-world haste. Some complaints are mild (manageable), but many say it's the ad mid-entry that breaks them.

product.title: Bought premium — ads came back after the update
product.minus: Paid premium systematically breaks after each update: ads come back, premium resets, and the only workaround is to uninstall and reinstall the app without updating. People openly call it fraud given that they paid.

product.title: Backup is manual Google Drive only — people lose years of data when changing phones
product.minus: No automatic cloud and no login on a new device: users don't realize backup must be turned on manually, switch phones, and lose all their years of transactions. Even those who set up Google Drive sometimes find auto-backup silently failing, needing manual runs.

product.title: No cross-device sync — couples can't run a budget together
product.minus: The most common request: sync between phone, tablet, and across Android and iPhone. One account doesn't work on multiple devices even with the same email, so couples can't keep shared expenses in one place.

product.title: No automatic SMS bank-parsing — the top wish of manual-entry users
product.minus: Logging is fully manual, and many trust the data because of it, but a huge share wish for automatic transaction reading from bank SMS — it would save tons of time. For those who have SMS parsing, it breaks over phone language or just doesn't fire.

product.title: Double-entry accounts deliver serious tracking of income, expenses and transfers
product.plus: Under the minimalist shell is real bookkeeping: multiple accounts, transfers between them, transparent double-entry. For those who know debit/credit, it reads as a full accounting tool, not just an expense notepad.

product.title: Subcategories exist, but their totals are never summed anywhere
product.minus: You can create subcategories within a category, but the app only shows the parent category's total, not the sum per subcategory. To find out how much went to Transport inside Other, users hit a wall — there's no subtotal and no nesting deeper than one level.

product.title: Multi-currency works for trips, but breaks when changing the main currency
product.minus: For a one-off trip with several currencies it's smooth — set rates, get totals. But the moment you need to change the main currency (moved countries, picked wrong at setup), exchange rates recalculate old transactions so all balances go wrong, and you can't just change the currency without losing data.

product.title: Editing an amount wipes the whole number instead of one digit — a maddening detail
product.minus: You can't delete a single digit when editing an amount — the app wipes the whole number and makes you retype it. There's no copy-paste either. Against otherwise convenient entry, this small thing irritates people the most.

product.title: Strong on spending control, but hides wealth growth: savings and investments look like money is gone
product.minus: For discipline and daily spending control the app is excellent, but money moved into savings or investments is treated as gone — real net-worth growth stays invisible. There's no unified view combining cash, savings and assets into one historical trajectory, and holdings like stocks and crypto must be updated manually.

product.title: Free with no forced subscription — a thing people love on its own
product.plus: The core features are fully usable for free with no pressure to subscribe, and users praise this as a standalone point — some buy premium out of gratitude and for the long haul, not because they're forced to.

product.title: Lifetime license revoked overnight with no warning
product.minus: People who bought a "lifetime" premium years ago suddenly find it gone after an update and are pushed onto a paid subscription — no email, no warning.

product.title: Update logs you out and password reset never arrives
product.minus: After the update users are logged out and can't get back in: the password-reset email never arrives, and there's no sign-up button in the app.

product.title: Years of financial records wiped by the update
product.minus: Users lose 3-6 years of accumulated history: after logging back in the account is empty, and restoring from backup simply doesn't work.

product.title: Support is silent on every request
product.minus: Emails to support go unanswered for weeks: even paid-license holders who attach receipts and GPA numbers get no reply at all.

product.title: New subscription price is several times the old one
product.minus: The subscription arrived priced many times higher than the old one-off purchase — for a budgeting app this feels like a slap in the face.

product.title: Basic everyday features locked behind the paywall
product.minus: Even basic actions became paid: adding a spend to your main wallet, keeping more than one account or category, or exporting your own data.

product.title: Currency conversion broke: everything recalculated 1-to-1
product.minus: After the update multi-currency tracking broke — all past foreign-currency operations were retroactively recalculated at 1:1, making the stats meaningless.

product.title: Cloud sync was first removed, leaving local backup only
product.minus: The main reason people bought premium — syncing across devices — was at one point cut without warning and replaced with local backup only, costing people their data when switching phones.

product.title: Clean, fast interface — the reason people love it
product.plus: Despite the scandal, the app itself is praised for a thoughtful, light, uncluttered interface: logging spends is fast and the spending picture is clear at a glance.

product.title: No bank linking — data stays on your phone
product.plus: Part of the appeal is that it doesn't connect to your bank accounts and keeps your finances local, with nothing sent to someone else's server.

product.title: For the lucky ones, license and data restore via a workaround
product.plus: Some users did get their lifetime access and data back: export a backup, clear Play Store cache, reinstall and sign in with the same Google account — the developer honored the old purchases.

product.title: Top request — attach a receipt photo to a transaction
product.minus: The most common request from happy users is the ability to attach a photo or scan of a receipt to an expense — a feature that's persistently missing.

product.title: The app is nearly impossible to find in the Play Store
product.minus: After returning to the store the app stopped showing up in search — fans complain they can't recommend it to friends and suspect a shadow ban.

product.title: Autofill fires intermittently and misses password fields
product.minus: The most common pain: autofill works one moment and not the next, fails to detect input fields, and forces users to manually copy login and password. For the core reason people install a manager, that defeats the whole point.

product.title: Search removed from the autofill screen — you can't link a login anymore
product.minus: A recent update removed the search button during autofill: when the manager picks the wrong login, you can no longer find and insert the right one manually — you have to leave the app and copy fields by hand. Many openly threaten to switch.

product.title: Keeps demanding the master password and ignores the PIN you set
product.minus: The app repeatedly asks for the master password instead of the PIN or biometrics you configured, even mid-session. You used to be able to sign in without exposing the master password — now you must type it over and over, which is both insecure and maddening.

product.title: Forced accessibility-service consent blocks you out of the app
product.minus: After an update a notice about the “optional” accessibility autofill appears, but the only button is “Accept”: refuse it and you can't open the app at all, locked away from your own passwords.

product.title: Crashes on launch and freezes on a range of Android devices
product.minus: On newer Android handsets (Xiaomi, OnePlus, Samsung) the app crashes right at startup or freezes after login, and neither reinstalling nor clearing the cache helps — access to passwords disappears entirely.

product.title: Nagging review-prompt pop-ups get in the way of actual use
product.minus: The “rate us” dialog pops up exactly when someone is urgently trying to grab a password — even after repeated “not now” taps. It reads as poor UX.

product.title: Forget the master password and you're permanently locked out
product.minus: If the master password suddenly stops being recognized or is forgotten, there's no reset: the site only offers an emailed hint, you can't sign in on a new device, and you can't even delete the account. Several users lost access to all their accounts, including crypto wallets.

product.title: Broken sync strands new passwords — and your work laptop access
product.minus: Saved passwords and authenticator codes sometimes fail to sync across devices, and self-hosters report that updates break Vaultwarden login. One user updated a work password, it didn't sync, and they were locked out of their own laptop.

product.title: Open source with zero-knowledge encryption of your vault
product.plus: The headline reason for the love: the project is open source, transparent, and encrypts everything on-device — passwords, usernames, notes, custom fields — so the service itself has zero knowledge of your vault. For a password manager, that's the very foundation of trust.

product.title: The free tier covers everything an average person needs
product.plus: The free version is powerful, ad-free, and fully featured — many buy a subscription just to support the devs rather than out of need. The paid plan, meanwhile, is described as remarkably cheap.

product.title: Seamless sync across every OS, device and browser
product.plus: When it works, cross-platform is the killer feature: one encrypted vault syncs across macOS, Windows, Linux, Android and iOS and every browser, plus a web vault and portable access. Sharing household logins via organizations and folders is easy.

product.title: Self-hosting via Vaultwarden — a haven for control and privacy
product.plus: Power users love being able to stand up their own Bitwarden or Vaultwarden server and keep passwords entirely under their own control; paired with Tailscale the Android client runs essentially flawlessly. That same community reacts sharply to news about the new CEO and the fate of the free tier.

product.title: A years-trusted password generator that just keeps working
product.plus: The loyalty backbone — people keep every password here for 5–10 years without a single failure, prize the strong generator, and value that it “just works” and stays out of the way. For many it's cheaper than their old LastPass or Roboform with no loss of features.

product.title: Android autofill is the core pain: it doesn't trigger, forcing manual copy-paste
product.minus: Dozens of users report the app stops detecting login and password fields — especially in Chrome, Brave and Firefox — so instead of the promised autofill they have to open 1Password itself and copy the password by hand. Many note it used to work and has degraded over the past year.

product.title: Biometrics break down: it demands the long master password every time despite a configured fingerprint
product.minus: A very common complaint: after some update, fingerprint or face unlock simply stops working, and the app asks for the long master password over and over — even with "never require" set in settings. Reinstalling and re-enrolling fingerprints usually doesn't help.

product.title: A sharp price hike (30-50% at once) is driving longtime subscribers to Bitwarden and Proton Pass
product.minus: An email announcing a 30-50% price jump in one shot was the last straw for many loyal users. They name specific alternatives — Bitwarden, Proton Pass, Google Password Manager — and leave, especially since free options do the same job.

product.title: The app hangs on unlock: an endless spinner instead of access to passwords
product.minus: A distinct cluster: the app simply won't open — after entering the password or fingerprint, an endless spinner just turns, the screen stays blank, and the only fix is force-stopping and restarting. For a password manager this is critical: people are locked out exactly when they need the password.

product.title: Best-in-class for cross-platform sync: one password works across every device and OS
product.plus: The main reason people stay and pay: flawless vault sync across Windows, macOS, Linux, Android and iOS, plus browser extensions. Families praise shared vaults, developers love the CLI and env integration. It's the reliability that earns forgiveness for the bugs.

product.title: When autofill works it feels "magical": one-click login changes daily life
product.plus: Those who have autofill set up correctly describe it as magic: one button fills login, password, even clicks sign-in. The strong-password generator, card storage and 2FA in one place — users call it life-changing and can't imagine going back to manual passwords.

product.title: Bolting AI into a paid security product reads as a betrayal of trust
product.minus: Some subscribers learned about AI being added from the same price-hike email — and judged it an unacceptable lapse for a security product. For them, "paying for AI" in a password manager is a reason to migrate, not stay. Many ask for at least an off-by-default toggle.

product.title: Support is slow and phone-less: only tickets and auto-replies when access is lost
product.minus: When something breaks — and the stakes are access to every password at once — support is slow, there's no phone line, and replies are often automated. Users feel abandoned at the critical moment and lose trust in a service they handed everything to.

product.title: The "secret key" and re-login system turns switching devices into a lockout nightmare
product.minus: The secret-key plus QR-on-new-device security model trips many up: switching phones leaves people locked out, the QR won't scan, and they're left responsible for a key file for years. Security so tightly wound that it blocks access to your own passwords.

product.title: Creating a new item forces the wrong type ("Identity" instead of "Login") with no way to fix it
product.minus: A specific UX bug: when signing up on a new site, the app decides to create an "Identity" rather than a "Login", and the type can't be changed. You have to leave the form, manually open 1Password, copy the URL and create the entry separately — exactly the chore the manager is supposed to remove.

product.title: The move from a v7 purchase to a v8 cloud subscription reads to many as "holding data hostage"
product.minus: Longtime owners of the one-time-purchase version 7 (and earlier) feel cheated: the "lifetime" license no longer works, export is buried, and the only path forward is the paid cloud subscription. To them it turned an honest product into a money grab.

product.title: Family plan and sharing are a genuine strength: safely share logins with loved ones
product.plus: Families and couples single out shared vaults: you can safely share logins, keep some items private by choice, and a travelling partner keeps access to accounts. For many the family plan alone is why they stay and find the subscription worth it.

product.title: The free tier vanished without warning — locking passwords behind a paywall
product.minus: Dozens of long-time users report the same arc: there was a free plan, it was quietly trimmed, then removed entirely. Without a subscription the app won't even let you view your own passwords — only export to CSV or pay. People call it ransom and holding data hostage.

product.title: Sudden account lockout while the paid subscription is still active
product.minus: A recurring story: payment went through and is confirmed in Google Play, yet the app suddenly claims the plan is "expired" and blocks access across all devices with no warning. People have the receipts and an active subscription — and are still locked out of their own password vault.

product.title: No support: a chatbot that can't find your account, and no human anywhere
product.minus: When something breaks, there's nowhere to turn: the AI bot answers in templates, claims no account exists for that email, and refuses to connect you to a human unless you're a paying member. But to pay you first need to log in — which is the exact problem. A closed loop.

product.title: Autofill has decayed: it no longer fires, forcing manual copy-paste
product.minus: The core feature broke for many, especially on Android. The prompt doesn't pop up over the keyboard, or it pops up but fills nothing. The result: open the app, copy username and password, switch back, paste. A password manager reduced to mere storage.

product.title: Constantly demands the master password — sometimes 6-7 times an hour
product.minus: The app asks for the master password over and over, even right after you've entered it, and won't keep you logged in on the phone. Biometrics often fail and fall back to manual entry. For a tool meant to save time, it becomes a constant ordeal.

product.title: Data loss: passwords vanish, accounts "deleted", no recovery
product.minus: The worst scenario for a password vault: people update or lose a phone — and lose 10+ years of passwords. Some get an email saying "your account has been deleted" while paid through year-end. Some watch half their logins vanish, replaced by strangers' old passwords.

product.title: Deleting your account is nearly impossible — needs a browser and extension
product.minus: Want to leave? Not so fast. You can't delete the account from your phone — you must install a browser extension on a computer, and even that often fails. And if you've already been logged out, deletion is unavailable entirely — your data stays with the company forever.

product.title: Prices jumped sharply and legacy plans were killed — VPN and extras forced on you
product.minus: Loyal users on old cheap plans are pushed onto a single expensive tier ($60/year, more elsewhere), bundling in VPN, dark-web monitoring and identity protection many don't want. Competitors like Bitwarden cost a third as much, and people are leaving.

product.title: Older devices abruptly declared unsupported — with no warning
product.minus: Long-time customers are cut off from their vault when their phone or tablet is declared "too old" with no notice. Since the only way in is the app (web access was removed), that means total loss of access to passwords — sometimes after 9 years of loyalty.

product.title: Web access removed — everything now goes through a clumsy browser extension
product.minus: You used to be able to log into the Dashlane website directly; now nothing works without the installed extension. Managing the family plan, adding people, accessing data from a computer — all funnel through an extension that's blocked on many work machines or simply clunky.

product.title: For the years-long faithful — a reliable, convenient vault that saves time
product.plus: Despite the wave of anger, there's a large happy core: people have kept Dashlane for 5-10+ years, praising the clean interface, cross-platform reach, strong-password generation, and the peace of mind of having everything in one place. For them it's an indispensable tool that's saved them more than once.

product.title: When support does come through — it rescues access in hopeless situations
product.plus: Amid the complaints there are also stories where a real agent genuinely helped: restored access after a lost email and 2FA via a rigorous identity check, answered a question, offered a good deal to retain the customer. A minority, but these show good support is possible here.

product.title: Autofill is the core promise and the core pain: it rarely fires
product.minus: Users pile up complaints that autofill works one time in five or worse: they end up opening the app and copy-pasting credentials by hand, which defeats the whole point of a password manager. The problem persists across browsers, keyboards and settings — people have tried everything.

product.title: The app hangs and won't open — locking people out of their own passwords
product.minus: A frequent grievance: the app crashes on launch or hangs forever on the Nord logo, and suddenly your only password vault is unreachable. Reinstalling doesn't help, and a useless «something went wrong» often appears. On some firmware (HyperOS, MIUI, Android 16) it's a black screen and total failure.

product.title: Cross-device sync breaks — passwords don't make it across
product.minus: A password made on the phone may never show up on the tablet or PC — not in 15 minutes, not in weeks. People are forced to dig out a laptop to find an entry missing from the mobile app. Sync used to work — updates broke it.

product.title: The Nord-account coupling spawns extra passwords and login loops
product.minus: A password manager that forces you to remember several passwords at once: a master password, a Nord-account password and a VPN one. It regularly kicks you out to a browser to verify your identity, and the process loops endlessly. The paradox: the Nord-account password lives inside the very vault you can't open without it.

product.title: Biometrics and quick unlock turn themselves off, forcing the master password
product.minus: After updates, fingerprint unlock vanishes — the option simply disappears from settings, leaving only the manual master password. Some are fully logged out every day and asked for an emailed code instead of a fingerprint, turning quick access into a multi-step ordeal.

product.title: Account recovery is a dead end: forget the master password, lose everything
product.minus: Lose your master password or recovery code and support won't restore your data — the only «fix» offered is wiping the entire vault. Backup codes often don't work, and identity verification demands data the person no longer has access to.

product.title: Support is deaf: canned replies, an AI bot on a loop and refusal to help
product.minus: Paying customers spend weeks unable to cancel, change their email or delete their account — support sends links to videos, asks the same question three times and won't connect them to a human. Several escalated to a card dispute because there was no other way to stop the charges.

product.title: A paywall and pushy upsells: basic features moved into Premium
product.minus: People resent that using a second device, the authenticator and other basics got locked behind a subscription, while the interface is plastered with «upgrade» banners. The real price after the discount hook has to be hunted down on the website, and many feel milked.

product.title: Digits and letters are indistinguishable: 0/O and l/I blur when reading a password
product.minus: An update removed the digit highlighting (or left it only in edit mode), so when typing by hand you can't tell a zero from an O, or a lowercase L from an uppercase I. To read a password you must enter edit mode and risk accidentally overwriting it.

product.title: No offline mode: with no internet, the password vault is unreachable
product.minus: Several users discovered that with no connection the app kicks them back to the login screen and won't show passwords — which is critical on a plane or abroad. For a password manager, many see this cloud dependency as fundamentally wrong design.

product.title: When it works — a clean, fast, pleasant vault people love for years
product.plus: Happy users praise the clean interface, speed and sense of reliability for years on end: everything in one place, easy to add and find passwords. Many switched from LastPass, Keeper, RoboForm or Google and find NordPass noticeably better and cheaper.

product.title: The breach and dark-web scanner — a feature people stay for
product.plus: The built-in breach scanner and dark-web monitor come up again and again as a favourite feature: it warns in time about compromised accounts, passwords and emails, including old breaches. For some, this — not the password storage — became the main value.

product.title: Price and the Nord ecosystem bundle — a strong reason to switch
product.plus: Many came for the attractive price (especially bundled with NordVPN) and stayed satisfied: importing passwords was easy and the feature set richer than their previous manager. For Nord ecosystem users, one unified security service is a real plus.

product.title: Prices jacked 100-300% in a single cycle, no explanation and no loyalty discount
product.minus: The single biggest driver of churn: people paid $15/year for 10-15 years, then got an email bumping it to $40-70 with no new features. Long-timers aren't grandfathered, deals go only to new sign-ups, and loyal users bail for Bitwarden and open-source.

product.title: Once the subscription lapses your data is held hostage: no editing, deleting, or exporting
product.minus: After cancelling, the free tier is read-only: you can't add, edit, or delete a record. Even exporting your own passwords is paywalled, so you can't leave for a competitor without paying first. Users flatly call it ransom and a scam.

product.title: Mobile-browser autofill works only intermittently, especially after updates and in Samsung Internet/Chrome
product.minus: Autofill is praised on desktop, but on phones Keeper Fill fails to detect login/password fields, doesn't work in Samsung Internet, breaks after updates, and forces manual copy-paste of passwords — itself a security risk.

product.title: You can't reach support without a paid subscription — even to fix a billing problem
product.minus: A vicious loop: you got double-charged or your subscription didn't activate, but you can't contact support because the system treats you as a free user. Emails go unanswered for weeks and replies are canned.

product.title: Billing trap: auto-renews three weeks early, charges after cancellation, hard no on refunds
product.minus: Auto-renewal fires three weeks before expiry, users get billed years after cancelling, and a strict no-refund/30-day policy blocks refunds even on double charges. Double and phantom charges through Google Play are routine.

product.title: The app crashes on launch after recent updates, only fixed by endless reinstalls
product.minus: After the late-2025 updates the app stops opening: it crashes on launch and only a reinstall helps, and only for a day or two. For a password manager you reach for at a critical moment, that's especially painful.

product.title: Constantly demands you re-enter the master password and sign in — sometimes three or four times in a row
product.minus: The extension and app re-prompt for the master password every couple of days, autofill won't fire without manually opening the app, and the browser makes you log in several times over. Users themselves flag this as a security risk.

product.title: Nagging upsells and ad notifications for add-ons you can't turn off
product.minus: Even paying subscribers get constant prompts to buy dark-web monitoring and storage, plus push ads that can't be disabled — users say they're effectively paying to be served ads.

product.title: Years of rock-solid reliability and security — the reason long-time users stay
product.plus: The core strength: people keep passwords, crypto seed phrases, and documents here for 5-15 years, sync across every device just works, and there's a genuine sense the data is truly safe. Many call Keeper the best manager they've tried.

product.title: When support does engage, it's fast, human, and account-saving
product.plus: A counterpoint to the complaints: those who reach a real person praise them by name (Clariece, Rene, Dann) — recovering accounts after a lost master password, fixing double charges, and instead of canned replies setting up a call that traced the bug to a specific Chrome version.

product.title: Duplicate records: the app spawns password copies and loses shared entries on the family plan
product.minus: After updates and on import Keeper creates two or three copies of the same entry, prompts to save what's already saved, and on the family plan shared records suddenly stop being shared — discovered at the worst possible moment.

product.title: Web checkout is blocked in many countries — you're forced to renew only through app stores
product.minus: In India, Thailand, Singapore, Egypt the site refuses payment ("Website checkout is not available for your country") and pushes you to the Google/Apple store, where prices are higher with no proper invoices or payment flexibility. For long-time customers it's a sudden loss of renewal access.

product.title: Android autofill is the core pain: it fires rarely and unpredictably
product.minus: Even with everything configured and Proton set as default, autofill simply doesn't show up when you need it: it skips the field, vanishes before you can tap, or stays silent on most sites and apps — forcing people to copy-paste credentials by hand.

product.title: Fills only one field: username yes, password no
product.minus: A recurring pattern: autofill drops in the username but not the password (or vice versa), then offers to "update" the entry and saves a duplicate with only half the data. Multi-page logins don't work at all.

product.title: Proton's privacy and the all-in-one subscription are the main reason people stay
product.plus: People come for the Swiss jurisdiction, open source, end-to-end encryption, and the fact that Proton doesn't sell their data. One annual bill covering VPN, mail, drive and passwords is the argument that keeps them even when the app misbehaves.

product.title: The app logs you out on its own — and the passwords are gone for good
product.minus: The scariest scenario: after a long stretch of biometric unlock the app suddenly demands the master password no one remembers. With no recovery phrase, access is gone and support shrugs — people lose dozens of saved passwords.

product.title: "Could not create login" — you can't save a new password
product.minus: For a chunk of users the basic act of saving is broken: the app offers to save a password but on "Save" throws "unable to create entry" / "could not create login" with no reason given. Existing entries still edit fine.

product.title: Duplicates multiply, and there's no way to merge them
product.minus: The app saves the same account multiple times, fails to recognise a password change, and offers no merge — leaving people to clean hundreds of duplicates by hand. It also flags false "duplicates" where a login simply has two addresses.

product.title: Basic organisation is paywalled: no folders, custom fields or icons
product.minus: It grates that elementary things are paywalled or just missing: custom fields are paid, the promised folders still aren't out, and you can't set your own categories, colours or icons. Everything ends up in one jumbled pile.

product.title: The free tier is generous — and that wins people over
product.plus: Many switch from Dashlane, Bitwarden, Google and Samsung Pass and are stunned by how much is free: password generator, notes, email aliases, unlimited devices. "Best free password manager I've tried."

product.title: Email aliases (SimpleLogin) are the killer feature that keeps people
product.plus: Built-in throwaway email aliases you can disable or trash whenever you like are, for many, the deciding factor. Together with built-in 2FA, it makes Proton Pass their primary manager.

product.title: A clean, pleasant UI — noticeably sleeker than Bitwarden
product.plus: Even people frustrated by the features praise the looks: the interface gets called slick, clean and prettier than Bitwarden's. For many it lends a premium feel to simple daily use.

product.title: Passkeys are advertised but barely work
product.minus: Passkeys let people down: on some phones Google pops up instead of Proton, on Android 12 the feature is unavailable, and without FIDO CXP/CXF the keys are locked into the vault with no export — vendor lock-in that Dashlane and 1Password already solved.

product.title: Import/export is tied to the desktop — you can't set it up on a phone alone
product.minus: To move passwords in you need a desktop browser extension — there's no built-in import/export in the app itself. For anyone without a PC that's a blocker, and people keep asking for in-app backup and transfer.

product.title: When it works, it "just works" and stays out of the way
product.plus: For a portion of users it's smooth sailing: autofill fires, PC-to-phone sync is seamless, and the app stays out of the way until needed. Migrating to a new phone was effortless for them.

product.title: Nagging "save password?" prompts with no per-app off switch
product.minus: The app pops up offering to save a password where none is being typed (and stays silent where one is), keeps nagging to save other authenticators' codes like MS Authenticator — and there's no "never save for this app" option.

product.title: Sync lags, or needs the app force-killed to update
product.minus: New and edited entries take ages to appear on other devices, sometimes never syncing at all. Some people have to kill the app and wipe its storage just to force a sync through.

product.title: The «lifetime» Pro license was retroactively downgraded, with Premium pushed on top
product.minus: Users who bought Pro «for life» years ago found features moved into a new paid Premium tier, and are now asked to buy yet another lifetime license. It reads as a bait-and-switch and is the number-one reason people are leaving for Bitwarden or KeePass.

product.title: Autofill keeps breaking — especially on Android, Firefox and Samsung
product.minus: The most frequent technical complaint: autofill stops working after updates, fills only the username but not the password, and breaks in Firefox and Chrome for months. For a password manager this kills the core use case, forcing manual copy-paste.

product.title: The killer feature — vault stored in your own cloud/NAS, not the developer's servers
product.plus: The most-loved reason to stay: data lives wherever you choose — Google Drive, OneDrive, your own NextCloud, a NAS — not in an Enpass database. After the LastPass breach this is, for many, the decisive privacy argument.

product.title: The free tier is useless: a 25- (or 10-) item cap that even shows random entries
product.minus: The free cap was cut to 25 — for some just 10 — items, and those items show up at random, so you can't find the password you need. Some users suddenly found their previously «unlimited» vault clamped down to 25.

product.title: Cross-platform support that just works: Windows, Mac, Linux, Android, iOS
product.plus: Long-term users praise seamless operation across every OS at once — Windows, Linux, Mac, Android, iPad. For many it's the best cross-platform manager they found after a long search.

product.title: A buy-once lifetime license instead of an endless subscription — the core money win
product.plus: People choose Enpass specifically for the one-time purchase: no never-ending monthly fee like Bitwarden or 1Password. Many moved here when 1Password went subscription-only.

product.title: Ads and pushy «buy Premium» banners inside an already-paid app
product.minus: Paying users are furious at constant upsell screens and a red subscription-nag banner that can't be dismissed. Having paid full price, they feel attacked by ads.

product.title: Vault syncing constantly fails — Wi-Fi, Dropbox, OneDrive, Google Drive
product.minus: Wi-Fi sync needs reconnecting every couple of months, Dropbox won't link, OneDrive drops out, Google Drive reports «cancelled by user». Those who refuse to push passwords to the cloud are left without sync entirely.

product.title: The app crashes when viewing and searching passwords
product.minus: Frequent crashes when opening an entry or searching — especially on Android and Chromebook, where the app sometimes won't even launch after an update. For long-time fans this became the last straw.

product.title: Import from other managers is broken or missing — migrating in is nearly impossible
product.minus: There's no proper import: entries must be added by hand one at a time, and when import does run it assigns the wrong templates. It turns away new users at the very first step.

product.title: A dangerous catch-22: re-activation and master-password prompts lock you out of your own data
product.minus: Sudden re-activation demands (the code goes to an email whose password is inside Enpass), daily master-password nagging, and «lost» licenses leave people locked out of their own vault. It's described as ransomware.

product.title: Support replies with canned templates or goes silent — license disputes drag on for weeks
product.minus: Support either never replies or sends the same canned response. Users have to prove with invoices, repeatedly, that they paid for a license — only for it to be downgraded again 20 days later.

product.title: Backup produces zero-byte files and won't restore
product.minus: Several updates in a row broke backup: files are created at zero bytes, restore fails, and the master password stops working after reinstall. For an app trusted with vital data this is critical.

product.title: Stable and reliable for years — a manager people trust daily
product.plus: A large core of loyal users has kept Enpass for 5-7+ years without trouble, opens it many times a day, and rates it best in class. Simple, clear, never loses passwords.

product.title: Flawless on desktop, painful on the phone
product.minus: The same users praise the desktop build and curse the mobile one: on Android it won't pick up logins, won't autofill, and degrades into a clumsy manual password lookup.

product.title: The vault outlives every device you own
product.plus: The core reason for 10-to-20-year loyalty: long passwords collapse into one master password, sync across every device, and survive every phone and computer swap.

product.title: The app insists on being a browser
product.minus: Instead of showing the saved login, the mobile app drags you to the website or googles your query — the built-in browser infuriates people who only wanted to grab a password.

product.title: Autofill pops up whenever it feels like it
product.minus: The login prompt shows up half the time at best; more often you have to dig out the credentials by hand — especially inside Android apps rather than the browser.

product.title: Password generator plus breach alerts
product.plus: Beyond storage, users value the strong-password generator and the warnings about compromised or reused passwords — it turns the manager into a hygiene tool, not just a vault.

product.title: Unquestioned trust in its security
product.plus: Across decades users recall no breaches, and the master password plus biometrics and cloud backup gives a sense of full control — there's even emergency access for heirs in case of death.

product.title: Biometrics and login break for no reason
product.minus: Login fails on a correct password, the emailed OTP screen vanishes when you switch to your mail app, or biometrics simply stops working — and support doesn't fix it.

product.title: Recent updates break the app
product.minus: Recent updates cause freezes on load and error messages; a separate gripe is a new version that chimes on every action with no way to silence it, even via notification settings.

product.title: Browser integration keeps falling out
product.minus: Integration with Firefox, DuckDuckGo and certain sites on Android either doesn't work or forces you to pick the password manually for each login — the app stops recognizing pages.

product.title: Cheaper for newcomers than for loyalists
product.minus: Long-time users resent that renewal discounts go to newcomers: to get the good price you have to re-register with a new email address.

product.title: Sync sometimes loses passwords
product.minus: Though sync is usually praised, for some users data doesn't make it across devices: a saved password simply never shows up on the phone.

product.title: Replaces the password notebook for non-techies
product.plus: Even non-technical users master it quickly and value that it ends passwords-on-scraps-of-paper; the address and card form-filling is called a lifesaver that saves hours.

product.title: Autofill works only half the time — you end up opening the app and copying the password by hand
product.minus: The core job — filling in passwords — fires inconsistently. Users say they have to open the app, find the entry and paste manually, which defeats the entire point of a password manager.

product.title: Constantly signs you out and demands the master password over and over
product.minus: The app logs people out again and again and forces the master password several times a day — even with biometrics on. The same phone gets flagged as a "new device."

product.title: Forget the master password and you lose the whole vault — there is no recovery
product.minus: If the master password is forgotten or suddenly stops being accepted, there's no way back: every recovery method (OTP, passkey, emailed code) fails and a decade of passwords is gone for good.

product.title: Support is locked behind login — exactly when you can't log in
product.minus: To contact support you must be logged in — but the people who need help are the ones who can't log in. Even paying users can't reach a human, and chat bounces them to a "you're not logged in" screen.

product.title: The data breach broke the one core promise — "zero-trust"
product.minus: Users point directly at the vault breach: data leaked, URLs turned out unencrypted, and trust in a product whose only job is security collapsed. Many leave specifically over this.

product.title: Useless offline — it hides your passwords exactly when you lose internet
product.minus: The app stops showing passwords when the connection drops, even if you were already authenticated. It hits hardest on a plane, where you need a password to get online in the first place.

product.title: Basic mobile-app access got pushed behind a paywall
product.minus: You used to use both phone and computer for free — now you must pick one device type or pay. Users call it a shakedown and walk away.

product.title: Every update makes the app worse — textbook "enshittification"
product.minus: Long-time users describe a downward arc: things that worked for years break after each update — biometrics, the notes window, the password editor. People openly call it product decay.

product.title: Drops compatibility with phones it ran fine on for years
product.minus: Paying users suddenly get "not compatible with your device" on the same phone the app ran on for years — Android 10/11 support was cut, and people demand refunds.

product.title: Charges money after cancellation and for long-dead accounts
product.minus: Users report unauthorized charges: billed a year after last use, money taken from a card whose details the company shouldn't have, renewals on a cancelled subscription.

product.title: Clutters the vault with duplicate entries for the same account
product.minus: The app spawns several entries for one site (sometimes up to six), there's no easy way to merge them, and the built-in duplicate finder stopped detecting them — the vault turns into a mess.

product.title: For long-time users it's a memory lifesaver and a shared family password vault
product.plus: Those for whom it works value the cross-device access, strong-password generation, and family sharing. People with memory issues and families sharing one account are especially grateful.

product.title: A loyal subset simply never hits the problems everyone else complains about
product.plus: Dozens of multi-year users say it runs smoothly and trouble-free for them for years. Some explicitly note they see the negative reviews but don't experience those issues themselves.

product.title: "No internet connection" on master password — even though the network is fine
product.minus: By far the most common complaint: entering the master password throws a "no internet" error while Wi-Fi and mobile data work fine. The same account logs in on the web — so it's an app bug, not the connection.

product.title: Years of saved passwords vanish at once, with no warning
product.minus: People open the app to an empty vault or "0 passwords": everything built up over years gone after an update. No recovery, no heads-up beforehand.

product.title: The SMS login code never arrives on a new device — locking the whole account
product.minus: Logging in on a new phone needs an SMS code that never arrives, and "resend" returns a server error. With no backup verification method, users get fully cut off from their passwords.

product.title: Support is paywalled — and the broken login won't even let you open a ticket
product.minus: You can only reach support with a paid subscription, and the form makes you log in first — but login is exactly what's broken. Free users end up at a bot that just links the paywalled section.

product.title: The mobile app won't sync with the browser and desktop
product.minus: Desktop and the extension work, but the phone lags behind: new passwords don't pull through and some entries never arrive. Out-of-sync passwords get rejected — making the vault useless on the go.

product.title: You can't change the master password: every attempt hits a connection error
product.minus: Changing the master password fails with a "connection error" or "unknown error" in both the app and the web. The only way out is a reset that wipes every saved record.

product.title: Dark mode breaks autofill: white text on a white background
product.minus: In dark mode the autofill popup renders as white text on a white background, so you can't tell which login you're picking. It hits recent Samsung Galaxy phones hardest after a OneUI update.

product.title: Autofill works only half the time — you end up copying by hand
product.minus: The login popup appears inconsistently, and the app fails to recognise some fields as password fields at all. So you open the app separately and copy-paste the password by hand.

product.title: Free, on every device, ad-free — the reason people stay for years
product.plus: The core reason for the love: a full password manager for free, syncing across phone, PC and browser, with no ads. Many have used it 4-6 years and are amazed it's still not paid.

product.title: Simple, friendly interface — easy even for beginners
product.plus: For those whose setup didn't break, the praise is about simplicity: a clear interface, fingerprint unlock, auto-generated passwords and notes per entry. They specifically note it isn't intimidating — good for first-time password-manager users.

product.title: A built-in 2FA authenticator, all in one app
product.plus: Some users value that it stores both passwords and 2FA codes together — a replacement for Microsoft or Google Authenticator. Keeping everything in one app across devices is the draw.

product.title: No import or export — you can't move in, and you can't get your passwords out
product.minus: There's no way to bring passwords in from another manager, nor to export your own out of Avira. So newcomers can't migrate in, and victims of a glitch can't even rescue their data to CSV.

product.title: Real-time shared lists are the heart of the app for families
product.plus: The number-one thing users love: spouses, kids, even a short-term lodger all see and edit one list at once, with change notifications — nothing gets forgotten or bought twice.

product.title: Recipe-to-shopping-list import is the standout killer feature
product.plus: Importing recipes from almost any site into a standardized ingredients-to-steps view, adding all ingredients to the list in one tap, and auto-rescaling by servings — this is what pushes many to pay.

product.title: Auto-categorizing by department kills the backtracking
product.plus: The list sorts items into departments and the department order can be arranged to match your own store's layout — the end of doubling back and walking in circles.

product.title: Cross-platform sync just works across iPhone and Android
product.plus: Lists sync seamlessly between iOS and Android, which matters for mixed-phone households — for many that alone justifies the subscription.

product.title: The free tier is genuinely useful on its own
product.plus: A chunk of users stay on the free version for years and find it complete: lists, sharing and sending to the store work unpaid, and the upgrade feels like a bonus rather than a ransom.

product.title: Forced sign-up right at startup drives people away
product.minus: No demo and no guest mode: the first launch demands an account, and some people find it invasive and uninstall on the spot without ever trying it.

product.title: Basic essentials locked behind the subscription frustrate users
product.minus: Entering your own prices, starter lists and other small things are paywalled, and people find it absurd to pay for such elementary features.

product.title: Google Assistant voice input is broken
product.minus: Voice-adding items via Google Assistant stopped working due to platform changes; Alexa still holds, but Android users who relied on dictating items are disappointed and saddened.

product.title: Disappearing items and odd categorizing undermine trust
product.minus: Some users complain items vanish halfway round the store or get accidentally crossed off before reaching the cart, and the auto-categories sometimes miss (grapes aren't vegetables).

product.title: Years of reliability and stability keep people loyal
product.plus: Many report using the app for years — some over a decade — praising its stability, steady meaningful updates and ongoing developer support, a rare kind of trust in a long-lived app.

product.title: Versatile beyond groceries — one app for every kind of list
product.plus: People run far more than groceries in it: packing and camping lists, home-and-garden chores, movies to watch, life goals, workout checklists — it stretches well beyond the store.

product.title: Weak export and thin local-store integration
product.minus: There's no mass export, which makes some users ready to leave, and store-ordering integration is largely US-only — users elsewhere want links to their own local delivery services.

product.title: Store-layout categories are the core reason people love it
product.plus: People keep separate lists per store and arrange categories to match the aisles — turning the app from a note into a walking route through the store.

product.title: Shared family lists are the killer feature that keeps people
product.plus: Spouse and kids add and check off items in one shared list — for many it's an indispensable household tool, especially when shopping separately.

product.title: Not just groceries — a universal list engine for everything
product.plus: People keep lists for travel, camping, gifts, passwords, TV shows, and chores — the app grew into a personal reminder system for everything.

product.title: Saved prices and running total help keep the budget
product.plus: Saved prices and a running total while shopping let users see the bill in advance — no surprises at checkout.

product.title: Intrusive ads and survey nags — even for paying Pro users
product.minus: Full-screen ads and a survey on every launch hit the very people who long ago bought the ad-free version — the new owner is monetizing what's already paid for.

product.title: Lag on check-off — tapping a checkbox registers seconds later
product.minus: Checking off a bought item lags 4-5 seconds, so people double-tap and check off the wrong thing — the core in-store action becomes punishing.

product.title: Sync loses data — wipes categories and reverts to old lists
product.minus: Sync deletes categories, updates shared lists slowly, or reverts to an old version — you stop being able to trust the shared list.

product.title: Auto-categorization breaks — items fall to Uncategorized and breed categories
product.minus: Familiar items suddenly drop into Uncategorized, auto-categories multiply and can't be deleted, and the slightest name variation breaks the layout — exactly the feature people came for.

product.title: Duplicates and phantom items — deleted things come back, history bloats
product.minus: The same item duplicates dozens of times, deleted entries reappear on their own, and history bloats to hundreds of repeats until the app crashes — forcing manual cleanup.

product.title: Accidental removal — a stray tap deletes an item with no confirmation
product.minus: A stray tap removes an item, and the delete-all button sits right where the thumb rests — with no confirmation, the whole list can get wiped mid-shop.

product.title: Mandatory account and tracking — for what was a simple checklist
product.minus: You now can't make a list without signing up and consenting to always-on tracking, with options like 'only while using' greyed out — people leave rather than hand over data for a shopping list.

product.title: Region lock cut off long-time users outside the US and Canada
product.minus: A sudden 'outside the service area' error locked users in Australia, and even inside the USA, out of the web and app — years of loyalty erased without warning.

product.title: Updates and new phones wipe years of accumulated lists
product.minus: Auto-updates delete all lists and categories, and migrating to a new phone fails — forcing a new account and re-entering everything, losing years of accumulated data.

product.title: Crashes, freezes, and UI overlapping the phone's system buttons
product.minus: The app crashes randomly and hangs the phone, and after an update the UI extends under the nav buttons and status bar — making the top and bottom controls unusable.

product.title: Barcode scanner abandoned — promised for years, nothing changes
product.minus: Barcode scanning, once a loved feature, doesn't work or fails to move items to the main list — users have asked for years while developers stay silent.

product.title: Autocorrect rewrites your item into a completely different product
product.minus: The single most common pain: you type "barbecue sauce" and get "Apple sauce", "A1 Steak Sauce" becomes a steak, "bag" turns into "bagel", "Nüsse" into "Noix". You can't switch it off, and Enter won't just keep exactly what you typed.

product.title: You can't delete or edit an item
product.minus: The most basic operation — removing an accidentally added item or renaming it — is simply missing for many users. Only the description is editable, not the name itself, and you're stuck with the wrong entry on your list.

product.title: List sharing doesn't work — the link just dumps you in the store
product.minus: The app's headline feature — a shared list — fails to start for many: the invite link opens the Play Store instead of adding the person to the list. Without shared access the whole point of the app collapses.

product.title: The perfect real-time shared list for a family
product.plus: When sharing does work it's the beloved feature: the whole family adds items and they appear for everyone instantly. Spouses walk different aisles, see what's already been bought, and shop in half the time.

product.title: Icons and the visual list are what users love most
product.plus: Visual people adore that each item gets an icon, is sorted by category and colour-coded — you barely need to read the labels. The clean, beautiful interface gets called the best on the market.

product.title: Free and ad-free — a rarity users treasure
product.plus: Many are won over that all features are free, with no subscriptions or paywalls, and no intrusive ads. People say they'd even be happy to pay — that's how useful it is.

product.title: No "bought" state — an item is either on the list or off it
product.minus: There's no third state: an item is either on the list or gone. People want to tick "got it" while shopping without deleting the entry, so they can reuse the same list every week.

product.title: You can't set the app language separately from the system
product.minus: The app language is hard-tied to the phone language: keep the system in English and "Knoblauch" silently becomes "garlic". Many miss their native language (Spanish, Portuguese, Greek) or a product database that isn't in theirs.

product.title: The watch app (Wear OS / Galaxy Watch) barely works
product.minus: Many install the app specifically for the watch, only to find the list doesn't show up or sync, with no categories or sort order matching the phone. On some watches it's declared unavailable entirely.

product.title: Login, account and password reset — a wall of bugs
product.minus: It grates that a simple list needs an email and account, and Google login freezes on a new phone. Password reset is broken in a loop: the email link goes to the Play Store and back to the login screen — you can never recover the account.

product.title: Notification spam: ads, "don't forget the berries", confirm your email
product.minus: Notifications turn into spam: hourly Billa ads, pointless reminders about items not on the list, a permanent red "confirm your email" badge. There are only two categories, and both bury you in junk.

product.title: You can't create your own categories to match the store layout
product.minus: The preset categories don't match a specific store's aisles, and you can't create your own — items from different aisles get lumped into one bucket. There's also no manual sort to follow your route through the store.

product.title: Each item eats half the screen — the list is hard to read
product.minus: The item tiles are huge: only a few entries fit on screen, forcing a lot of scrolling. There's no way to shrink the tile size, and the overall information density is low.

product.title: The constant request: a home-screen widget
product.minus: One of the most frequent asks even from fans is a home-screen widget showing the list. The advertised widgets are missing from the Android/iOS widget lists, and many would bump to five stars the moment one ships.

product.title: A lifeline for people with ADHD and forgetfulness
product.plus: A distinct and heartfelt thank-you comes from people with ADHD: instead of calls and notes, family just add what they need to the list, and the user only has to check it. The app genuinely lifts the guilt of forgetting.

product.title: The AI assistant is forced and can't be turned off
product.minus: The number-one pain: a plain list app got an AI assistant bolted on, with a banner over every list, on by default and impossible to disable. People who for years just wanted to jot down groceries are leaving en masse because the AI can't be removed.

product.title: Full-screen ads hijack the screen right at the checkout
product.minus: Ads evolved from banners into unskippable full-screen videos that pop up after adding an item or closing a list — exactly when you're standing at the checkout. After the AI, this is the biggest trigger for leaving.

product.title: Real-time shared lists are the core reason people love it
product.plus: The heart of the app: family and partners keep one shared list, and whoever's near a shop sees updates instantly. This is what keeps even angry users — getting a whole family to agree on a new app is a nightmare.

product.title: Simplicity and ease of use — what they love most
product.plus: The core flow is polished: jot it down fast, tick it off, don't forget. The interface is pleasant, the learning curve minimal, and even elderly users and people with memory issues rely on it.

product.title: Versatility: not just groceries, but any kind of list
product.plus: Users unexpectedly treasure that their whole life lives in the app: lists for travel, packing, home improvement, gifts, movies, even business inventory. Reusable lists and purchase history deepen the attachment.

product.title: The app adds items to your list without consent
product.minus: A particularly insidious pain: a "you've added an item" pop-up loads faster than the Add button and can't be declined, so junk lands in your list and you spend half the shop deleting it. It hits even paying users.

product.title: Endless consent prompts to share data with dozens of partners
product.minus: A shopping-list app repeatedly demands consent to share data with 54–55 partners, including geolocation, and asks again after every update even when you refuse. For many it's a dealbreaker before they ever use it.

product.title: Prices and running totals help you stay on budget
product.plus: Adding prices and seeing a running total before checkout is an underrated strength: people budget, estimate the weekly shop, and track spending right inside the app.

product.title: Auto-categorization and item memory keep the list tidy
product.plus: The app auto-sorts items into categories and pulls frequently bought things from history without creating duplicates. This speeds up recurring lists and keeps shopping grouped by store aisle.

product.title: Premium doesn't stop the ads or the upsell nagging
product.minus: Those who paid for "no ads" feel cheated: upgrade banners, AI, and subscription offers still hit them, and a second device on the same premium account still shows ads. On top of that, they removed the one-time purchase in favor of a subscription.

product.title: Feature creep made the interface slow and laggy
product.minus: Animations, AI, and ads have weighed down a simple checklist: the interface lags, the app freezes and crashes, and ads drain the battery. Opening to a summary screen instead of the lists adds extra clicks.

product.title: Lists and sync sometimes get lost when switching phones
product.minus: A painful trust failure: after switching phones or a reset, lists don't carry over, shared lists stop updating in real time, and the widget throws an error. For an app holding "your whole life," data loss stings especially hard.

product.title: Responsive support sometimes wins users back — they added an AI toggle
product.plus: A bright spot amid the backlash: support genuinely replies and fixes issues, and a "Show AI Suggestions" toggle appeared in list settings that hides the hated banner. Some users restored their stars precisely because of this.

product.title: Real-time list sync across all the family's devices is the core reason people love it
product.plus: One person adds items from home while the other is already heading to the store, and they show up instantly; you can 'divide and conquer' the aisles and cross things off live. It just works, the same across Android and iPhone.

product.title: Ads secretly add products to your list and lie that a household member added them
product.minus: The app inserts products on its own, labeling them 'someone in your household tapped add', even when only husband and wife have access and nobody did it. People call home to ask who added it, and end up leaving for an 'honest' app.

product.title: The December UI redesign ('new look') is seen as a clear step backwards
product.minus: Long-time users are furious about the update: it was simple and clean, now it's messy and crowded. Buttons don't look like buttons, the colors are poor, and many beg to bring back the old look or roll back entirely.

product.title: Indispensable for the family: anyone can add to the shared list and nothing gets forgotten
product.plus: The whole household keeps one list, and any family member adds what's needed at any time. The main shopper no longer comes home having forgotten things — you keep adding while they're on the way to the store.

product.title: Categories/aisles and store-layout sorting turn shopping into a route
product.plus: The app auto-sorts items into groups (produce, deli), and groups can be ordered to match your supermarket — you can even make categories by aisle number. You move through the store strictly down the list.

product.title: Moving the input field and search to the middle/bottom of the screen made adding items awkward
product.minus: After the update the input field can't be pinned at the top: with a long list you have to scroll all the way to the bottom to add something. Moving the search bar and an extra '+' in the middle of the list annoy people most.

product.title: Crossed-off items aren't deleted but move down — easy to bring back for repeat shops
product.plus: A beloved mechanic: cross an item off and it's saved at the bottom, so next time you just un-cross it. Perfect for regular runs and rare lists like Thanksgiving.

product.title: No prices and no running total — the most common feature request
product.minus: Users keep asking to enter item prices and see a total with tax, to compare and stay on budget. Competitors like Out of Milk do this, which makes OurGroceries feel feature-light by comparison.

product.title: Alexa/Google Assistant integration keeps breaking after updates
product.minus: Voice-adding via Alexa was a favorite feature, but after Alexa 2.0 the 'Alexa, ask Our Groceries to add…' command no longer works. Google Assistant doesn't recognize the app as a target either — leaving only slow manual entry.

product.title: Product photos, notes and a barcode scanner — nice extras people pay for
product.plus: You can attach a photo to each item to avoid confusion in the store, add notes and quantity, and the barcode scanner and photo recognition work better than you'd expect.

product.title: Versatile far beyond groceries: recipes, trip packing, gifts, checklists
